rows: Vulva or clitoris (7610, incl. vulvovaginitis); Vagina (7611); Cervix (7612); Uterus (7613, disease/injury/adhesions); Fallopian tube (7614, incl. PID); Ovary (7615, disease/injury/adhesions)

General Rating Formula (DC 7610–7615): · • 30%: Symptoms not controlled by continuous treatment. · • 10%: Symptoms that require continuous treatment. · • 0%: Symptoms that do not require continuous treatment. (Note: 7610 covered vulva only prior to May 13, 2018).

Retained 30 / 10 / 0% General Rating Formula for Disease, Injury, or Adhesions of Female Reproductive Organs; expanded DC 7610 to vulva or clitoris (including vulvovaginitis) and clarified DC 7615 Note covering ovarian dysfunction, dysmenorrhea, and secondary amenorrhea.

• Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS): Rated under DC 7615 (10%/30% for continuous metformin/OCP/spironolactone) PLUS unbundle secondary DC 7913 Type 2 Diabetes (Endocrine Diff), DC 7828 cystic acne, DC 7101 HTN, obesity -> DC 6847 OSA (VAOPGCPREC 1-2017), and DC 7632 FSAD / infertility! · • Cervical Dysplasia / HPV (DC 7612): Check LEEP/cone biopsy stenosis/incompetence & MST markers (Playbook 16).
Uterus and both ovaries, removal of, complete (Total abdominal/laparoscopic hysterectomy + bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy TAH-BSO)
100% for 3 months after removal; thereafter 50% + mandatory SMC(k).
Retained 100% for 3 months after removal -> 50% permanent schedular floor + mandatory SMC(k) (§ 3.350(a)(1)).

Also audit surgical menopause sequelae: secondary osteoporosis (DC 5013), hot flashes/vasomotor, mood disorder (§ 4.130), abdominal scar (DC 7801/7804), and post-hysterectomy vault prolapse (DC 7621) or stress incontinence (§ 4.115a)!
Uterus, removal of, including corpus (Total or supracervical hysterectomy with one or both ovaries preserved)
100% for 3 months after removal; thereafter 30% + mandatory SMC(k).
Retained 100% for 3 months after removal -> 30% permanent schedular floor + mandatory SMC(k) (§ 3.350(a)(1)).
Under VAOPGCPREC 5-89, a prior non-SC elective tubal ligation never bars SMC(k) upon SC removal of the uterus under DC 7617 or DC 7618!
Ovary, removal of (Oophorectomy)
100% for 3 months after removal; thereafter: · • Complete removal of both = 30% + SMC(k) · • Removal of one with or without partial removal of the other = 0% (no SMC(k) if remaining ovary functions).

Retained 100% for 3 months -> 30% + SMC(k) (both removed) or 0% (unilateral). Added Explicit Paired-Organ Note (83 FR 15068): If 1 ovary is removed due to SC cause and the 2nd ovary is absent or nonfunctioning from non-service-connected causes, assign 30% (+ SMC(k))!

Codifies 38 U.S.C. § 1160(a) / 38 C.F.R. § 3.383 paired-organ protection directly inside DC 7619! (Note: 100% 3-month convalescent floor does not apply to unilateral chemical/natural nonfunction without surgical removal).
Ovaries, atrophy of both, complete (Premature ovarian insufficiency / chemo or radiation ovarian failure)
20% + mandatory SMC(k) (§ 3.350(a)(1)(ii)).
Retained 20% + mandatory SMC(k).
Common secondary residual of antineoplastic chemotherapy, pelvic radiation, or autoimmune polyglandular syndrome (DC 7912).
7621 (and retired 7622–7623)
Complete or incomplete pelvic organ prolapse due to injury, disease, or surgical complications of pregnancy (cystocele, rectocele, enterocele, uterovaginal or vaginal vault prolapse)

• DC 7621 Uterus, prolapse: Complete (through vagina & introitus) = 50%; Incomplete = 30%. · • DC 7622 Uterus, displacement of: Marked displacement & frequent or continuous menstrual disturbances = 30%; With adhesions & irregular menstruation = 10%. · • DC 7623 Pregnancy, surgical complications of: With rectocele or cystocele = 50%; Relaxation of perineum = 10%.

Unified DC 7621 (83 FR 15068, 15069): Complete or incomplete pelvic organ prolapse due to injury, disease, or surgical complications of pregnancy = flat 10% (Note: VA's Final Rule abandoned its proposed POP-Q Stage II floor—so any complete or incomplete prolapse warrants 10%, plus mandatory separate evaluation of GU, digestive, and skin symptoms!) · • DC 7622 & DC 7623: [Removed May 13, 2018].

CRITICAL GRANDFATHERING & UNBUNDLING RULES: · 1. 38 U.S.C. § 1155 Shield: Pre-May 13, 2018 running 50% or 30% awards under DC 7621–7623 cannot be reduced to 10% under the 2018 schedule! · 2. Why 83 FR 15068 Set DC 7621 at 10%: VA set structural prolapse at 10% specifically because functional bladder, bowel, and skin impairments are rated SEPARATELY (Esteban): always stack § 4.115a Voiding Dysfunction / Stress Incontinence (60% appliance or >4 pads/day; 40% 2–4 pads/day; 20% 1 pad/day) AND DC 7332 Rectum & Anus Impairment / Fecal Incontinence (10%–100%, System 07 Digestive Diff)!
Fistula, urethrovaginal (or vesicovaginal)
100%: Multiple urethrovaginal fistulae. · 60%: Requiring appliance or absorbent materials changed > 4x/day. · 40%: Absorbent materials changed 2–4x/day. · 20%: Absorbent materials changed < 2x/day.
Retained 100 / 60 / 40 / 20% schedule.
Mirrors § 4.115a voiding-dysfunction absorbent-material tiers plus a standalone 100% tier for multiple urethrovaginal fistulae!
Malignant neoplasms of gynecological system (ovarian, cervical, uterine/endometrial, vaginal, vulvar, fallopian)
(Pre-2018 covered both GYN and breast malignancies!) 100% active disease/treatment + 6 months post-cessation -> mandatory VA exam + § 3.105(e) -> rate residuals.

Narrowed to gynecological malignancies (breast moved to DC 7630): 100% active + 6 months post-cessation of surgical, radiation, antineoplastic chemotherapy, or other therapeutic procedure -> mandatory VA exam + § 3.105(e) Foster notice -> rate residuals (DC 7617–7620, lymphedema DC 7121, scars, bladder/bowel, SMC(k)).
PACT Act 38 U.S.C. § 1120(b)(2)(H): Every DC 7627 gynecological malignancy is a presumptive burn-pit / Gulf War / post-9/11 reproductive cancer (Playbook 15)!
Benign neoplasms of gynecological system (uterine leiomyomas / fibroids, benign ovarian cysts/teratomas, polyps)
(Added 60 FR 19851): Rate according to impairment in urinary or gynecological systems (§ 4.115a or DC 7610–7615).

Expanded Residual Note (83 FR 15068): Rate chronic residuals according to impairment of function due to scars, lymphedema, or disfigurement and/or gynecological (DC 7610–7620), urinary (§ 4.115a), or digestive (§ 4.114) involvement!

Uterine fibroids (DC 7628) frequently cause bulk bladder frequency (§ 4.115a 10%–40%), constipation (DC 7319), iron-deficiency anemia from menorrhagia (DC 7720 [former DC 7700 pre-Dec. 9, 2018 — watch DC 7720 Note evaluating blood-loss anemia under the underlying bleeding code!]), or require total hysterectomy (DC 7618 = 100% 3 mos -> 30% + SMC(k))!
Endometriosis

(Added 60 FR 19851): · • 50%: Lesions involving bowel or bladder confirmed by laparoscopy, pelvic pain or heavy/irregular bleeding not controlled by treatment, and bowel or bladder symptoms. · • 30%: Pelvic pain or heavy/irregular bleeding not controlled by treatment. · • 10%: Pelvic pain or heavy/irregular bleeding requiring continuous treatment for control. · • Note: Diagnosis must be substantiated by laparoscopy; 50% requires laparoscopic confirmation of bowel/bladder lesions.
Retained verbatim 50% / 30% / 10% criteria AND retained the mandatory laparoscopy Note!

ACTIVE LAPAROSCOPY GATE TRAP: Until RIN 2900-AS39 (90 FR 47266, Oct. 1, 2025 — proposed / not finalized) is enacted as a Final Rule, current eCFR DC 7629 still requires laparoscopic confirmation! Whenever endometriosis was diagnosed clinically or by MRI/ultrasound without laparoscopy, immediately plead DC 7613/7615 (10%/30%) or § 4.20 analogy (Webb / Saunders) so VA cannot deny service connection!
Malignant neoplasms of the breast (female and male)
(Evaluated under DC 7627 prior to May 13, 2018).

Created May 13, 2018 (83 FR 15068): 100% active malignancy + 6 months post-cessation of surgical, radiation, antineoplastic chemotherapy, or other therapeutic procedure -> mandatory VA exam + § 3.105(e) Foster notice -> rate chronic residuals (DC 7626, scars DC 7801/7804, lymphedema DC 7121, shoulder/arm/wrist ROM, grip strength/nerve loss DC 8518, harvested reconstructive muscle flaps DC 5301–5320, and SMC(k))!
See Section 3.C for the adjuvant endocrine therapy (tamoxifen / aromatase inhibitors) 100% continuation dispute and mandatory multi-system post-cancer unbundling!

Benign neoplasms of the breast and other injuries of the breast (fibroadenoma, fibrocystic breast disease, mastitis, breast trauma, ruptured implant/capsular contracture from SC surgery, male gynecomastia)
(Evaluated by analogy under DC 7626 / 7628 prior to May 13, 2018).

Created May 13, 2018 (83 FR 15068): Rate chronic residuals according to impairment of function due to scars, lymphedema, or disfigurement (arm/shoulder/wrist ROM, grip strength, sensation, muscle harvesting) and/or under DC 7626.
Covers antipsychotic/spironolactone/endocrine-induced male gynecomastia (§ 3.310(a) secondary SC — yielding 30%–50% under DC 7626 if surgical mastectomy/excision significantly alters size or form!).
Female sexual arousal disorder (FSAD) (incl. female sexual interest/arousal disorder & genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder / dyspareunia)
(No dedicated VASRD code prior to May 13, 2018; claimed by analogy to DC 7610/7522).
Created May 13, 2018 (83 FR 15068): 0% schedular evaluation + mandatory review for statutory SMC(k) (38 U.S.C. § 1114(k); 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)(1) loss of use of a creative organ)!

MASSIVE UNDER-CLAIMED GOLDMINE: Mirrors male DC 7522 Erectile Dysfunction ($139.87/mo tax-free in 2026). Audit every female veteran on SSRIs/SNRIs (sertraline, fluoxetine, paroxetine, venlafaxine, duloxetine) for SC PTSD/MDD, or with MST, pelvic trauma/prolapse, endometriosis, or diabetes (DC 7913)!

title: Schedule of ratings—hematologic and lymphatic systems
summary: Published October 29, 2018, effective December 9, 2018 (RIN 2900-AO19), overhauling the Oct. 23, 1995 schedule (60 FR 49227; DC 7717 AL Amyloidosis 100% added Mar. 9, 2012 at 77 FR 6467): added Rai Stage 0 (0%) vs. Stage I–IV (100%) staging to DC 7703 CLL, extended DC 7715 NHL post-treatment 100% evaluation from 6 months to 2 years, added DC 7712 Multiple Myeloma (100% for 5 years with §§ 3.105(e) & 3.344(a)–(b) protection; smoldering/MGUS 0%), DC 7718 ET/PMF, DC 7719 CML (30/60/100% TKI tiers), DC 7720–7723 Anemias, DC 7724 Solitary Plasmacytoma, and DC 7725 MDS. CRITICAL ARCHIVAL CORRECTION: On October 11, 2022 (87 FR 61248, effective Oct. 11, 2022 and explicitly applicable retroactively as of December 9, 2018), VA corrected two omissions in DC 7718 by restoring 'for any of the following treatments:' in the 100% tier and 'or interferon treatment' in Note (2).

**§ 4.117 Schedule of ratings—hemic and lymphatic systems.**

**7700 Anemia, hypochromic-microcytic and megaloblastic, such as iron-deficiency and pernicious anemia:**
* Hemoglobin 5gm/100ml or less, with findings such as high output congestive heart failure or dyspnea at rest — **100**
* Hemoglobin 7gm/100ml or less, with findings such as dyspnea on mild exertion, cardiomegaly, tachycardia (100 to 120 beats per minute) or syncope (three episodes in the last six months) — **70**
* Hemoglobin 8gm/100ml or less, with findings such as fatigue, exertional dyspnea, tachycardia (90 to 100 beats per minute) or dizziness — **30**
* Hemoglobin 10gm/100ml or less, with occasional dizziness or fatigue — **10**
* Hemoglobin greater than 10gm/100ml, asymptomatic — **0**
* **Note:** Evaluate chronic residuals of pernicious anemia, such as dementia or peripheral neuropathy, separately.

**7702 Agranulocytosis, acute:**
* Requiring bone marrow transplant, or; requiring transfusion of platelets or red cells at least once every six weeks, or; infections recurring at least once every six weeks — **100**
* Requiring transfusion of platelets or red cells at least once every three months, or; infections recurring at least once every three months — **60**
* Requiring transfusion of platelets or red cells at least once per year but less than once every three months, or; infections recurring at least once per year but less than once every three months — **30**
* Requiring continuous medication for control — **10**
* **Note:** The 100 percent rating for bone marrow transplant shall be assigned as of the date of hospital admission and shall continue with a mandatory VA examination six months following hospital discharge. Any change in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter.

**7703 Leukemia:**
* With active disease or during a treatment phase — **100**
* Otherwise rate as anemia (code 7700) or aplastic anemia (code 7716), whichever would result in the greater benefit.
* **Note:** The 100 percent rating shall continue beyond the cessation of any surgical, radiation, antineoplastic chemotherapy or other therapeutic procedures. Six months after discontinuance of such treatment, the appropriate disability rating shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any change in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter. If there has been no recurrence, rate on residuals.

**7704 Polycythemia vera:**
* During periods of treatment with myelosuppressants and for three months following cessation of myelosuppressant therapy — **100**
* Requiring phlebotomy — **40**
* Stable, with or without continuous medication — **10**
* **Note:** Rate complications such as hypertension, gout, stroke or thrombotic disease separately.

**7705 Thrombocytopenia, primary, idiopathic or immune:**
* Platelet count of less than 20,000, with active bleeding, requiring treatment with medication and transfusions — **100**
* Platelet count between 20,000 and 70,000, not requiring treatment, without bleeding — **70**
* Stable platelet count between 70,000 and 100,000, without bleeding — **30**
* Stable platelet count of 100,000 or more, without bleeding — **0**

**7706 Splenectomy** — **20**
* **Note:** Rate complications such as systemic infections with encapsulated bacteria separately.

**7707 Spleen, injury of, healed.**
* Rate for any residuals.

**7709 Hodgkin's disease:**
* With active disease or during a treatment phase — **100**
* **Note:** The 100 percent rating shall continue beyond the cessation of any surgical, radiation, antineoplastic chemotherapy or other therapeutic procedures. Six months after discontinuance of such treatment, the appropriate disability rating shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any change in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter. If there has been no local recurrence or metastasis, rate on residuals.

**7710 Adenitis, tuberculous, active or inactive.**
* Rate under §§ 4.88c or 4.89 of this part, whichever is appropriate.

**7714 Sickle cell anemia:**
* With repeated painful crises, occurring in skin, joints, bones or any major organs caused by hemolysis and sickling of red blood cells, with anemia, thrombosis and infarction, with symptoms precluding even light manual labor — **100**
* With painful crises several times a year or with symptoms precluding other than light manual labor — **60**
* With painful crises 1 or 2 times a year — **30**
* Asymptomatic, established case in remission, but with identifiable organ impairment — **10**
* **Note:** Sickle cell trait alone, without a history of directly attributable pathological findings, is not a ratable disability. Cases of symptomatic sickle cell trait will be forwarded to the Director, Compensation Service, for consideration under § 3.321(b)(1) of this chapter.

**7715 Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma:**
* With active disease or during a treatment phase — **100**
* **Note:** The 100 percent rating shall continue beyond the cessation of any surgical, radiation, antineoplastic chemotherapy or other therapeutic procedures. Six months after discontinuance of such treatment, the appropriate disability rating shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any change in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter. If there has been no local recurrence or metastasis, rate on residuals.

**7716 Aplastic anemia:**
* Requiring bone marrow transplant, or; requiring transfusion of platelets or red cells at least once every six weeks, or; infections recurring at least once every six weeks — **100**
* Requiring transfusion of platelets or red cells at least once every three months, or; infections recurring at least once every three months — **60**
* Requiring transfusion of platelets or red cells at least once per year but less than once every three months, or; infections recurring at least once per year but less than once every three months — **30**
* Requiring continuous medication for control — **10**
* **Note:** The 100 percent rating for bone marrow transplant shall be assigned as of the date of hospital admission and shall continue with a mandatory VA examination six months following hospital discharge. Any change in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter.

**7717 AL amyloidosis (primary amyloidosis)** — **100**

**§ 4.117 Schedule of ratings—hematologic and lymphatic systems.**

**7702 Agranulocytosis, acquired:**
* Requiring bone marrow transplant; or infections recurring, on average, at least once every six weeks per 12-month period — **100**
* Requiring intermittent myeloid growth factors (granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) or granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) or continuous immunosuppressive therapy such as cyclosporine to maintain absolute neutrophil count (ANC) greater than 500/microliter (µl) but less than 1000/µl; or infections recurring, on average, at least once every three months per 12-month period — **60**
* Requiring intermittent myeloid growth factors to maintain ANC greater than 1000/µl; or infections recurring, on average, at least once per 12-month period but less than once every three months per 12-month period — **30**
* Requiring continuous medication (e.g., antibiotics) for control; or requiring intermittent use of a myeloid growth factor to maintain ANC greater than or equal to 1500/µl — **10**
* **Note:** A 100 percent evaluation for bone marrow transplant shall be assigned as of the date of hospital admission and shall continue with a mandatory VA examination six months following hospital discharge. Any change in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter.

**7703 Leukemia (except for chronic myelogenous leukemia):**
* When there is active disease or during a treatment phase — **100**
* Otherwise rate residuals under the appropriate diagnostic code(s).
* Chronic lymphocytic leukemia or monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (MBL), asymptomatic, Rai Stage 0 — **0**
* **Note (1):** A 100 percent evaluation shall continue beyond the cessation of any surgical therapy, radiation therapy, antineoplastic chemotherapy, or other therapeutic procedures. Six months after discontinuance of such treatment, the appropriate disability rating shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any change in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter. If there has been no recurrence, rate on residuals.
* **Note (2):** Evaluate symptomatic chronic lymphocytic leukemia that is at Rai Stage I, II, III, or IV the same as any other leukemia evaluated under this diagnostic code.
* **Note (3):** Evaluate residuals of leukemia or leukemia therapy under the appropriate diagnostic code(s).

**7704 Polycythemia vera:**
* Requiring peripheral blood or bone marrow stem-cell transplant or chemotherapy (including myelosuppressants) for the purpose of ameliorating the symptom burden — **100**
* Requiring phlebotomy 6 or more times per 12-month period or molecularly targeted therapy for the purpose of controlling RBC count — **60**
* Requiring phlebotomy 4–5 times per 12-month period, or if requiring continuous biologic therapy or myelosuppressive agents, to include interferon, to maintain platelets <200,000 or white blood cells (WBC) <12,000 — **30**
* Requiring phlebotomy 3 or fewer times per 12-month period or if requiring biologic therapy or interferon on an intermittent basis as needed to maintain all blood values at reference range levels — **10**
* **Note (1):** Rate complications such as hypertension, gout, stroke, or thrombotic disease separately.
* **Note (2):** If the condition undergoes leukemic transformation, evaluate as leukemia under diagnostic code 7703.
* **Note (3):** A 100 percent evaluation shall be assigned as of the date of hospital admission for peripheral blood or bone marrow stem cell transplant; or during the period of treatment with chemotherapy (including myelosuppressants). Six months following hospital discharge or, in the case of chemotherapy treatment, six months after completion of treatment, the appropriate disability rating shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any reduction in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter.

**7705 Immune thrombocytopenia:**
* Requiring chemotherapy for chronic refractory thrombocytopenia; or a platelet count 30,000 or below despite treatment — **100**
* Requiring immunosuppressive therapy; or for a platelet count higher than 30,000 but not higher than 50,000, with history of hospitalization because of severe bleeding requiring intravenous immune globulin, high-dose parenteral corticosteroids, and platelet transfusions — **70**
* Platelet count higher than 30,000 but not higher than 50,000, with either immune thrombocytopenia or mild mucous membrane bleeding which requires oral corticosteroid therapy or intravenous immune globulin — **30**
* Platelet count higher than 30,000 but not higher than 50,000, not requiring treatment — **10**
* Platelet count above 50,000 and asymptomatic; or for immune thrombocytopenia in remission — **0**
* **Note (1):** Separately evaluate splenectomy under diagnostic code 7706 and combine with an evaluation under this diagnostic code.
* **Note (2):** A 100 percent evaluation shall continue beyond the cessation of chemotherapy. Six months after discontinuance of such treatment, the appropriate disability rating shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any reduction in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter.

**7706 Splenectomy** — **20**
* **Note:** Separately rate complications such as systemic infections with encapsulated bacteria.

**7707 Spleen, injury of, healed.**
* Rate for any residuals.

**7709 Hodgkin's lymphoma:**
* With active disease or during a treatment phase — **100**
* **Note:** A 100 percent evaluation shall continue beyond the cessation of any surgical therapy, radiation therapy, antineoplastic chemotherapy, or other therapeutic procedures. Six months after discontinuance of such treatment, the appropriate disability rating shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any reduction in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter. If there has been no local recurrence or metastasis, rate on residuals under the appropriate diagnostic code(s).

**7710 Adenitis, tuberculous, active or inactive:**
* Rate under § 4.88c or 4.89 of this part, whichever is appropriate.

**7712 Multiple myeloma:**
* Symptomatic multiple myeloma — **100**
* Asymptomatic, smoldering, or monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) — **0**
* **Note (1):** Current validated biomarkers of symptomatic multiple myeloma and asymptomatic multiple myeloma, smoldering, or monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) are acceptable for the diagnosis of multiple myeloma as defined by the American Society of Hematology (ASH) and International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG).
* **Note (2):** The 100 percent evaluation shall continue for five years after the diagnosis of symptomatic multiple myeloma, at which time the appropriate disability evaluation shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any reduction in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) and § 3.344 (a) and (b) of this chapter.

**7714 Sickle cell anemia:**
* With at least 4 or more painful episodes per 12-month period, occurring in skin, joints, bones, or any major organs, caused by hemolysis and sickling of red blood cells, with anemia, thrombosis, and infarction, with residual symptoms precluding even light manual labor — **100**
* With 3 painful episodes per 12-month period or with symptoms precluding other than light manual labor — **60**
* With 1 or 2 painful episodes per 12-month period — **30**
* Asymptomatic, established case in remission, but with identifiable organ impairment — **10**
* **Note:** Sickle cell trait alone, without a history of directly attributable pathological findings, is not a ratable disability. Cases of symptomatic sickle cell trait will be forwarded to the Director, Compensation Service, for consideration under § 3.321(b)(1) of this chapter.

**7715 Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma:**
* When there is active disease, during treatment phase, or with indolent and non-contiguous phase of low grade NHL — **100**
* **Note:** A 100 percent evaluation shall continue beyond the cessation of any surgical therapy, radiation therapy, antineoplastic chemotherapy, or other therapeutic procedures. Two years after discontinuance of such treatment, the appropriate disability rating shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any reduction in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter. If there has been no recurrence, rate on residuals under the appropriate diagnostic code(s).

**7716 Aplastic anemia:**
* Requiring peripheral blood or bone marrow stem cell transplant; or requiring transfusion of platelets or red cells, on average, at least once every six weeks per 12-month period; or infections recurring, on average, at least once every six weeks per 12-month period — **100**
* Requiring transfusion of platelets or red cells, on average, at least once every three months per 12-month period; or infections recurring, on average, at least once every three months per 12-month period; or using continuous therapy with immunosuppressive agent or newer platelet stimulating factors — **60**
* Requiring transfusion of platelets or red cells, on average, at least once per 12-month period; or infections recurring, on average, at least once per 12-month period — **30**
* **Note (1):** A 100 percent evaluation for peripheral blood or bone marrow stem cell transplant shall be assigned as of the date of hospital admission and shall continue with a mandatory VA examination six months following hospital discharge. Any change in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter.
* **Note (2):** The term “newer platelet stimulating factors” includes medication, factors, or other agents approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration.

**7717 AL amyloidosis (primary amyloidosis)** — **100**

**7718 Essential thrombocythemia and primary myelofibrosis:**
* Requiring either continuous myelosuppressive therapy, or, for six months following hospital admission for any of the following treatments: peripheral blood or bone marrow stem cell transplant, or chemotherapy, or interferon treatment — **100**
* Requiring continuous or intermittent myelosuppressive therapy, or chemotherapy, or interferon treatment to maintain platelet count <500 × 10⁹/L — **70**
* Requiring continuous or intermittent myelosuppressive therapy, or chemotherapy, or interferon treatment to maintain platelet count of 200,000–400,000, or white blood cell (WBC) count of 4,000–10,000 — **30**
* Asymptomatic — **0**
* **Note (1):** If the condition undergoes leukemic transformation, evaluate as leukemia under diagnostic code 7703.
* **Note (2):** A 100 percent evaluation shall be assigned as of the date of hospital admission for peripheral blood or bone marrow stem cell transplant; or during the period of treatment with chemotherapy (including myelosuppressants) or interferon treatment. Six months following hospital discharge or, in the case of chemotherapy treatment, six months after completion of treatment, the appropriate disability rating shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any reduction in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter.

**7719 Chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) (chronic myeloid leukemia or chronic granulocytic leukemia):**
* Requiring peripheral blood or bone marrow stem cell transplant, or continuous myelosuppressive or immunosuppressive therapy treatment — **100**
* Requiring intermittent myelosuppressive therapy, or molecularly targeted therapy with tyrosine kinase inhibitors, or interferon treatment when not in apparent remission — **60**
* In apparent remission on continuous molecularly targeted therapy with tyrosine kinase inhibitors — **30**
* **Note (1):** If the condition undergoes leukemic transformation, evaluate as leukemia under diagnostic code 7703.
* **Note (2):** A 100 percent evaluation shall be assigned as of the date of hospital admission for peripheral blood or bone marrow stem cell transplant; or during the period of treatment with chemotherapy (including myelosuppressants). Six months following hospital discharge or, in the case of chemotherapy treatment, six months after completion of treatment, the appropriate disability rating shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any reduction in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105 of this chapter.

**7720 Iron deficiency anemia:**
* Requiring intravenous iron infusions 4 or more times per 12-month period — **30**
* Requiring intravenous iron infusions at least 1 time but less than 4 times per 12-month period, or requiring continuous treatment with oral supplementation — **10**
* Asymptomatic or requiring treatment only by dietary modification — **0**
* **Note:** Do not evaluate iron deficiency anemia due to blood loss under this diagnostic code. Evaluate iron deficiency anemia due to blood loss under the criteria for the condition causing the blood loss.

**7721 Folic acid deficiency:**
* Requiring continuous treatment with high-dose oral supplementation — **10**
* Asymptomatic or requiring treatment only by dietary modification — **0**

**7722 Pernicious anemia and Vitamin B12 deficiency anemia:**
* For initial diagnosis requiring transfusion due to severe anemia, or if there are signs or symptoms related to central nervous system impairment, such as encephalopathy, myelopathy, or severe peripheral neuropathy, requiring parenteral B12 therapy — **100**
* Requiring continuous treatment with Vitamin B12 injections, Vitamin B12 sublingual or high-dose oral tablets, or Vitamin B12 nasal spray or gel — **10**
* **Note:** A 100 percent evaluation for pernicious anemia and Vitamin B12 deficiency shall be assigned as of the date of the initial diagnosis requiring transfusion due to severe anemia or parenteral B12 therapy and shall continue with a mandatory VA examination six months following hospital discharge or cessation of parenteral B12 therapy. Any reduction in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter. Thereafter, evaluate at 10 percent and separately evaluate any residual effects.

**7723 Acquired hemolytic anemia:**
* Requiring a bone marrow transplant or continuous intravenous or immunosuppressive therapy (e.g., prednisone, Cytoxan, azathioprine, or rituximab) — **100**
* Requiring immunosuppressive medication 4 or more times per 12-month period — **60**
* Requiring at least 2 but less than 4 courses of immunosuppressive therapy per 12-month period — **30**
* Requiring one course of immunosuppressive therapy per 12-month period — **10**
* Asymptomatic — **0**
* **Note (1):** A 100 percent evaluation for bone marrow transplant shall be assigned as of the date of hospital admission and shall continue for six months after hospital discharge with a mandatory VA examination six months following hospital discharge. Any reduction in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter.
* **Note (2):** Separately evaluate splenectomy under diagnostic code 7706 and combine with an evaluation under diagnostic code 7723.

**7724 Solitary plasmacytoma:**
* Solitary plasmacytoma, when there is active disease or during a treatment phase — **100**
* **Note (1):** A 100 percent evaluation shall continue beyond the cessation of any surgical therapy, radiation therapy, antineoplastic chemotherapy, or other therapeutic procedures (including autologous stem cell transplantation). Six months after discontinuance of such treatment, the appropriate disability rating shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any change in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter. If there has been no recurrence, rate residuals under the appropriate diagnostic codes.
* **Note (2):** Rate a solitary plasmacytoma that has developed into multiple myeloma as symptomatic multiple myeloma.
* **Note (3):** Rate residuals of plasma cell dysplasia (e.g., thrombosis) and adverse effects of medical treatment (e.g., neuropathy) under the appropriate diagnostic codes.

**7725 Myelodysplastic syndromes:**
* Requiring peripheral blood or bone marrow stem cell transplant; or requiring chemotherapy — **100**
* Requiring 4 or more blood or platelet transfusions per 12-month period; or infections requiring hospitalization 3 or more times per 12-month period — **60**
* Requiring at least 1 but no more than 3 blood or platelet transfusions per 12-month period; infections requiring hospitalization at least 1 but no more than 2 times per 12-month period; or requiring biologic therapy on an ongoing basis (e.g., erythropoiesis-stimulating agents or myeloid growth factors) — **30**
* **Note (1):** If the condition progresses to leukemia, evaluate as leukemia under diagnostic code 7703.
* **Note (2):** A 100 percent evaluation shall be assigned as of the date of hospital admission for peripheral blood or bone marrow stem cell transplant, or during the period of treatment with chemotherapy, and shall continue with a mandatory VA examination six months following hospital discharge or, in the case of chemotherapy treatment, six months after completion of treatment. Any reduction in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter. If there has been no recurrence, residuals will be rated under the appropriate diagnostic codes.

trapTables.title: 1. Master Chronological Federal Register & Presumptive Ledger (1946–2026)
headers: Substantive Change Across 38 C.F.R. § 4.117 & Linked Part 3 Presumptions
rows: Enacted Era-1 § 4.117 (DC 7700–7715): hemoglobin-ladder DC 7700 Anemia, DC 7703 Leukemia, DC 7704 Polycythemia vera, DC 7705 Thrombocytopenia, DC 7706 Splenectomy (30% -> later 20%), DC 7709 Hodgkin's, DC 7714 Sickle cell anemia, and DC 7715 Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (59 FR 28260, June 1, 1994). (Multiple myeloma lacked a dedicated code prior to Dec. 9, 2018 and was rated by § 4.20 analogy.)
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (< Oct. 23, 1995): Governs pre-1995 CUE audits and early Nehmer staged periods for NHL (38 C.F.R. § 3.313, Vietnam service) and Hodgkin's (59 FR 5106, Feb. 3, 1994).

First Modern Hemic/Lymphatic Overhaul (Era 2): Retitled section; standardized DC 7700 Anemia hemoglobin cutoffs (<= 5g/100ml = 100% down to <= 10g/100ml = 10%); added DC 7716 Aplastic anemia; set DC 7706 Splenectomy at 20%; codified 100% active-disease + mandatory 6-month post-treatment VA exam notes across DC 7703, 7709, and 7715.

CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (Oct. 23, 1995 – Dec. 8, 2018): Crucially, under Era-2 DC 7703, both asymptomatic CLL ("watchful waiting") and TKI-treated CML received 100% as active incurable leukemias!

Added Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) (later expanded to all chronic B-cell leukemias, including hairy cell leukemia, at 75 FR 53202, Aug. 31, 2010) to 38 C.F.R. § 3.309(e) herbicide presumptions -> full § 3.816 Nehmer class retroactivity!
Nehmer Retroactive Herbicide (§ 3.816) & CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive: Any pre-Dec. 9, 2018 staged Nehmer period for diagnosed CLL (even Rai Stage 0!) commands 100%!
77 FR 6466 (pub. Feb. 8, 2012; RIN 2900-AN75) (disambiguated from FRA rule 77 FR 13978)

Created DC 7717 AL Amyloidosis (Primary Amyloidosis): Implemented VA's May 7, 2009 Agent Orange presumption (74 FR 21258) in Part 4 by assigning a permanent, flat 100% evaluation upon diagnosis with no scheduled future re-examination.
Nehmer Retroactive Herbicide (§ 3.816) & CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (>= Mar. 9, 2012): Rating SC AL amyloidosis below 100% or scheduling routine reduction exams is plain-text error.

Second Major Hemic/Lymphatic Overhaul (Era 3): Retitled "The Hematologic and Lymphatic Systems"; repealed DC 7700 and enacted etiology-specific anemias (DC 7720–7723); split DC 7719 CML (30%/60%/100% TKI tiers) from DC 7703; set asymptomatic Rai Stage 0 CLL / MBL at 0%; created dedicated DC 7712 Multiple myeloma (5-year 100% floor for symptomatic myeloma + § 3.344(a)–(b) protection vs. 0% smoldering/MGUS); added DC 7718 (ET/myelofibrosis), DC 7724 Solitary plasmacytoma, and DC 7725 MDS.

CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (>= Dec. 9, 2018): Running pre-Dec. 9, 2018 100% CLL and CML awards are statutorily protected against reduction under 38 U.S.C. § 1155 & § 3.951(a)! Pending claims straddling Dec. 9, 2018 receive Era-2 100% prior to Dec. 9, 2018 (Karnas / 83 FR 54250 applicability clause).
Added Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance (MGUS — DC 7712 0%) as a herbicide presumptive condition.

Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (>= Aug. 10, 2022): Excluded from § 3.816 Nehmer retroactivity (M21-1 VIII.i.2.B.1.c), UNLESS MGUS progressed to symptomatic DC 7712 Multiple Myeloma or DC 7717 AL Amyloidosis (both of which ARE full Nehmer conditions!).
87 FR 61248 (pub. & eff. Oct. 11, 2022; retroactively applicable as of Dec. 9, 2018)

Correcting Amendment to DC 7718: Fixed syntax/typographical omissions in the 100% evaluation criteria and Note (2) for Essential thrombocythemia and primary myelofibrosis, retroactively applicable to December 9, 2018.
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (applicable >= Dec. 9, 2018).

Enacted 38 C.F.R. § 3.320b, adding acute and chronic leukemias (DC 7703/7719), multiple myeloma including MGUS (DC 7712), myelodysplastic syndromes (DC 7725), and myelofibrosis (DC 7718) as PM2.5 burn-pit presumptive conditions for Gulf War / Post-9/11 veterans (Playbook 15).
Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (>= Jan. 10, 2025): Unlocks § 3.114(a) 1-year lookback + PACT § 1305 / § 3.33 retroactive survivor DIC re-evaluations!

trapTables.title: 2. Structural Overhaul Diff (Oct. 23, 1995 Era 2 vs. Dec. 9, 2018 Era 3, 83 FR 54250)
rows: Anemias (Former DC 7700 -> DC 7720–7723)

Single blanket DC 7700 (Anemia, hypochromic-microcytic and megaloblastic) rated strictly by static gm/100ml hemoglobin ladder + clinical signs (<= 5g = 100%; <= 7g = 70%; <= 8g = 30%; <= 10g = 10%; > 10g asymptomatic = 0%).

DC 7700 REPEALED. Replaced by four etiology/treatment-driven codes: · • DC 7720 Iron deficiency anemia (30%/10%/0% IV infusions vs. oral iron; secondary blood-loss excluded per Note!) · • DC 7721 Folic acid deficiency (10%/0%) · • DC 7722 Pernicious / Vitamin B12 deficiency anemia (100%/10% + separate CNS/neuropathy!) · • DC 7723 Acquired hemolytic anemia (100%/60%/30%/10%/0% immunosuppressives/transplant).

Liberalization for Medicated Veterans: Under Era 2, a veteran on lifelong B12 injections or oral iron whose medicated hemoglobin normalized above 10 g/dL got 0%; under Era 3 DC 7720–7722, continuous oral iron, high-dose folate, or B12 injections/nasal/sublingual therapy earns 10% regardless of normalized hemoglobin!
Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia (Former DC 7703 -> DC 7719)
Rated under DC 7703 Leukemia -> 100% throughout active disease or continuous treatment phase (including daily oral tyrosine kinase inhibitors [TKIs] like imatinib [Gleevec]).

Split into dedicated DC 7719 (CML): · • 100%: Stem-cell transplant or continuous myelosuppressive/immunosuppressive therapy. · • 60%: Intermittent myelosuppressive, OR TKI / interferon when NOT in apparent remission. · • 30%: In apparent remission on continuous molecularly targeted TKI therapy (blast crisis transforms back to DC 7703 100% per Note).

Massive § 3.951(a) Reduction Shield: Any veteran holding a running 100% DC 7703 rating for CML on December 8, 2018 CANNOT be reduced to 30% or 60% based on the creation of DC 7719 (38 U.S.C. § 1155; Playbook 05)!
Asymptomatic CLL (DC 7703 Rai Stage 0)
Rated 100% under DC 7703 even during asymptomatic "watchful waiting" (Rai Stage 0) without chemotherapy because CLL remained an active, unremitted hematologic malignancy (83 FR 54250, 54251).

DC 7703: Explicitly assigns 0% to asymptomatic CLL or monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (MBL) at Rai Stage 0; Rai Stages I–IV or any symptomatic/treated CLL receives 100% (+ 6-month post-treatment floor).

Huge Nehmer (§ 3.816) Staged-Rating Goldmine: In any retroactive Nehmer or § 3.156(c) CLL award reaching back before Dec. 9, 2018, Rai Stage 0 "watchful waiting" periods prior to Dec. 9, 2018 MUST be paid at 100% (+ grandfathered at 100% thereafter if continuously pending/awarded)!
Myeloproliferative & Pre-Leukemic Disorders (DC 7704, 7718, 7725)
Only DC 7704 Polycythemia vera (100%/40%/10%) and DC 7716 Aplastic anemia existed; MDS and primary myelofibrosis / essential thrombocythemia had to be rated analogously (§ 4.20) under 7716 or 7704.

Revised DC 7704 Polycythemia vera (100%/60%/30%/10% phlebotomy/biologics + separate thrombosis/stroke/gout/HTN); added DC 7718 Essential thrombocythemia & primary myelofibrosis (100%/70%/30%/0%, corr. 87 FR 61248) and DC 7725 Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) (100%/60%/30% — minimum 30% floor when ongoing biologic therapy or 1–3 transfusions/hospitalizations!).
Cross-check Camp Lejeune (§ 3.307(a)(7)(iii) MDS/aplastic anemia) and the Jan. 10, 2025 § 3.320b burn-pit IFR (MDS DC 7725 & myelofibrosis DC 7718)!
Plasma Cell Dyscrasias (DC 7712, 7717, 7724)
Multiple myeloma had NO dedicated diagnostic code prior to Dec. 9, 2018 (rated by § 4.20 analogy, e.g., 7799-7703 or 7799-7715); DC 7717 AL Amyloidosis (100% permanent added Mar. 9, 2012).

Added DC 7712 Multiple myeloma: 100% symptomatic (5-year post-diagnosis floor + explicit § 3.105(e) & § 3.344(a)–(b) protection under Note (2)!) vs. 0% asymptomatic/smoldering/MGUS (ASH/IMWG biomarkers per Note (1)); added DC 7724 Solitary plasmacytoma (100% + 6-month post-treatment floor); retained DC 7717 AL Amyloidosis (100% permanent).
Never leave DC 7712 MGUS at a bare 0% without auditing secondary paraproteinemic peripheral neuropathy, renal disease, anemia, and progression to DC 7712 (100%) or DC 7717 (100%)!

trapTables.title: A. Side-by-Side Mandatory 100% Duration & Post-Treatment Re-Evaluation Matrix
rows: Leukemia (Acute myeloid AML, acute lymphoblastic ALL, hairy cell, symptomatic CLL Rai I–IV; excludes CML 7719 & Rai 0 CLL)

100% during active disease or treatment phase + 6 months beyond cessation of any surgical, radiation, antineoplastic chemotherapy, or other therapeutic procedures. (Rai Stage 0 asymptomatic CLL / MBL = 0% post-Dec. 9, 2018).

Mandatory VA examination at 6 months post-treatment cessation; any reduction requires 60-day § 3.105(e) notice (Foster v. McDonough, 34 Vet. App. 338 (2021), though §§ 3.343/3.344 do not apply). Rate chronic chemo-induced peripheral neuropathy (DC 8520/8515), cardiomyopathy (DC 7020), cytopenias, fatigue, and psychiatric depression (§ 4.130) separately!
Hodgkin's lymphoma
100% with active disease or during treatment phase + 6 months after discontinuance of surgical, radiation, chemotherapy, or other therapeutic procedures.

Mandatory VA examination at 6 months + § 3.105(e) notice. Audit post-mantle-radiation secondary hypothyroidism (DC 7903), coronary/valvular heart disease (DC 7005/7000), pulmonary fibrosis (DC 6825), and bleomycin/vinblastine neuropathy!
Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) (Includes indolent/follicular, diffuse large B-cell, mantle cell, cutaneous T-cell mycosis fungoides, Waldenström's macroglobulinemia)

100% when there is active disease, during a treatment phase, OR with indolent and non-contiguous phase of low-grade NHL + TWO (2) YEARS after discontinuance of surgical, radiation, chemotherapy, or other therapeutic procedures!

CRITICAL 2-YEAR FLOOR TRAP: Unlike DC 7703/7709 (6 months), DC 7715 guarantees 100% for 2 full years post-treatment—AND low-grade/indolent non-contiguous NHL in "watch and wait" remains 100% indefinitely (unlike Rai 0 CLL)! Cutting NHL at 6 months is undebatable RO CUE (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive).
Multiple myeloma

100% for symptomatic multiple myeloma (CRAB end-organ features or ASH/IMWG myeloma-defining biomarkers per Note (1)), continuing for FIVE (5) YEARS after the diagnosis of symptomatic multiple myeloma (Note (2))! (Asymptomatic, smoldering, or MGUS = 0%).

CRITICAL 5-YEAR FLOOR + § 3.344 SHIELD: Under DC 7712 Note (2), 100% continues for 5 full years from diagnosis before mandatory VA examination, AND any reduction is explicitly subject to BOTH 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e) AND § 3.344(a) and (b) sustained-improvement stabilization protections! Even when MGUS or smoldering myeloma is rated 0%, separately rate paraproteinemic neuropathy, light-chain renal disease (DC 7530), pathologic vertebral/rib fractures, and secondary mood disorder.
AL Amyloidosis (primary amyloidosis)
Permanent flat 100% evaluation upon diagnosis (77 FR 6466, eff. Mar. 9, 2012; retained 83 FR 54250).

NO future examination scheduled. Immediately audit for 38 U.S.C. § 1114(s) (SMC(s)) (Bradley statutory 100% + 60%) or SMC(l)–(r) by separately evaluating amyloid restrictive cardiomyopathy (DC 7020), nephrotic syndrome (DC 7502), autonomic/peripheral neuropathy, and GI malabsorption (Playbook 12)!
Solitary plasmacytoma (Osseous or extramedullary)
100% during active disease or treatment phase (including radiation, surgery, chemo, or autologous stem-cell transplant) + 6 months after discontinuance (Note (1)).

Mandatory VA examination at 6 months + § 3.105(e) notice; rate skeletal/neurological/radiation residuals separately, and monitor closely (~50%+ risk) for progression to DC 7712 Multiple Myeloma (100%)!

trapTables.title: 4. Complete Non-Malignant & Myeloproliferative Schedule (DC 7702, 7704–7707, 7710, 7714, 7716, 7718–7723, 7725)
headers: Post-Dec. 9, 2018 (83 FR 54250 / 87 FR 61248) Evaluation Tiers & Key Practice Traps
rows: Agranulocytosis, acquired

• 100%: Requiring bone marrow transplant (+ 6 mos post-discharge + mandatory VA exam), OR infections recurring >= 1 every 6 weeks per 12-month period. · • 60%: Intermittent myeloid growth factors (G-CSF/GM-CSF) or continuous immunosuppressives (e.g., cyclosporine) to maintain ANC > 500/µL to < 1,000/µL; OR infections >= 1 every 3 months/yr. · • 30%: Intermittent myeloid growth factors to maintain ANC > 1,000/µL; OR infections 1 to < 4 times/yr. · • 10%: Continuous medication (e.g., prophylactic antibiotics) OR intermittent myeloid growth factor to maintain ANC >= 1,500/µL.
Polycythemia vera

• 100%: Stem-cell transplant or chemotherapy/myelosuppressants (+ 6 mos post-discharge/completion + mandatory VA exam per Note (3)). · • 60%: Phlebotomy >= 6 times/yr OR molecularly targeted therapy (e.g., ruxolitinib JAK1/2 inhibitor) to control RBC count. · • 30%: Phlebotomy 4–5 times/yr, OR continuous biologic/myelosuppressive/interferon therapy to maintain platelets < 200,000 or WBC < 12,000. · • 10%: Phlebotomy <= 3 times/yr OR intermittent biologic/interferon therapy. · • Note (1) Separate Stacking: Rate secondary hypertension (7101), gout (5017), stroke (8007–8009), DVT/pulmonary embolism (7121/6817), or erythromelalgia/pruritus (7825) separately! (Note (2): leukemic transformation -> DC 7703).
Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) (formerly Idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura)

• 100%: Requiring chemotherapy for chronic refractory thrombocytopenia; OR platelet count <= 30,000 despite treatment. · • 70%: Requiring immunosuppressive therapy; OR platelets > 30,000 to 50,000 with history of hospitalization for severe bleeding requiring IVIG, high-dose parenteral corticosteroids, and platelet transfusions. · • 30%: Platelets > 30,000 to 50,000 with mild mucous membrane bleeding requiring oral corticosteroids or IVIG. · • 10%: Platelets > 30,000 to 50,000, not requiring treatment. · • 0%: Platelets > 50,000 and asymptomatic, or in remission. (Note (1): Separately evaluate DC 7706 Splenectomy (20%) and combine with DC 7705!)
Splenectomy

Flat 20% evaluation. Note — Separate Residual Stacking (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive): Separately evaluate (1) any complications such as systemic infections with encapsulated bacteria (S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, H. influenzae), (2) Group XIX abdominal wall muscle injury (DC 5319: 0/10/30/50%) for penetrating combat trauma (Playbook 01, Muscle Injuries Diff), and (3) painful or large laparotomy scars (DC 7801/7802/7804) (Scars Diff)!
Spleen, injury of, healed (7707); Adenitis, tuberculous (7710)
• 7707: Rate for any peritoneal adhesions (DC 7301), muscle, or scar residuals. · • 7710: Rate under 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.88c or 4.89 nonpulmonary tuberculosis rules (System 04 Diff).
Sickle cell anemia

• 100%: >= 4 painful episodes/yr in skin, joints, bones, or major organs (hemolysis/sickling with anemia, thrombosis, infarction) with residual symptoms precluding even light manual labor. · • 60%: 3 painful episodes/yr OR symptoms precluding other than light manual labor. · • 30%: 1 or 2 painful episodes/yr (changed Dec. 9, 2018 from qualitative "repeated hemolytic sickling crises"). · • 10%: Asymptomatic, established case in remission, with identifiable organ impairment. · • Hereditary Disease Law (VAOPGCPREC 82-90 & 67-90; 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(c)): Sickle cell anemia (and thalassemia / hereditary spherocytosis / G6PD hemolytic anemia) is a compensable hereditary disease whenever clinical symptoms first manifest in service or undergo permanent in-service aggravation (O'Bryan v. McDonald, 771 F.3d 1376 (Fed. Cir. 2014)). By contrast, per DC 7714 Note, sickle cell trait alone, without a history of directly attributable pathological findings (e.g., exertional rhabdomyolysis, splenic infarction at altitude, or renal papillary necrosis), is not a ratable disability.
Aplastic anemia

• 100%: Stem-cell transplant (+ 6 mos post-discharge + exam); OR RBC/platelet transfusions >= 1 every 6 weeks/yr; OR infections >= 1 every 6 weeks/yr. · • 60%: Transfusions or infections >= 1 every 3 months/yr; OR continuous immunosuppressive therapy or newer platelet-stimulating factors (eltrombopag/romiplostim, per Note (2)). · • 30%: Transfusions or infections >= 1 per 12-month period. (Note: Post-Dec. 9, 2018 DC 7716 provides 100% / 60% / 30% active tiers—removing Era 2's 10% continuous-medication tier; cross-check § 3.309(a) 1-yr chronic & Camp Lejeune § 3.307(a)(7)!)
Essential thrombocythemia (ET) & primary myelofibrosis (Corrected 87 FR 61248, Oct. 11, 2022)

• 100%: Continuous myelosuppressive therapy, OR for 6 months following hospital admission for stem-cell transplant, chemotherapy, or interferon (+ mandatory VA exam per Note (2)). · • 70%: Continuous or intermittent myelosuppressive, chemotherapy, or interferon to maintain platelets < 500 x 10^9/L. · • 30%: Continuous or intermittent therapy to maintain platelets 200,000–400,000 or WBC 4,000–10,000. · • 0%: Asymptomatic (rate thrombotic/hemorrhagic/splenomegaly residuals separately; leukemic transformation -> DC 7703; Jan. 10, 2025 § 3.320b burn-pit presumption!).
Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS)

• 100%: Stem-cell transplant or requiring chemotherapy (azacitidine/decitabine, + 6 mos post-discharge/cessation + mandatory VA exam). · • 60%: >= 4 blood/platelet transfusions/yr OR >= 3 hospitalized infections/yr. · • 30%: 1–3 transfusions/yr, 1–2 hospitalized infections/yr, OR ongoing biologic therapy (epoetin/darbepoetin/lenalidomide/luspatercept). (Transformation to AML -> DC 7703 100%; Camp Lejeune & Jan. 10, 2025 § 3.320b burn-pit presumptive!)

title: Schedule of ratings—skin (General Rating Formula for the Skin & Non-Scar Dermatological Overhaul)
summary: Published July 13, 2018, effective August 13, 2018 (RIN 2900-AP27): codified § 4.118(a) route-of-administration definitions of systemic vs. topical therapy, § 4.118(b) non-overlapping skin combination rule, the General Rating Formula for the Skin (explicitly adding biologics, phototherapy, retinoids, photochemotherapy, and PUVA), a dedicated 100/60/30/10/0% schedule under DC 7817 Erythroderma, 1st/2nd/3rd-line tiers under DC 7825 Chronic Urticaria, updated DC 7826–7827, and a 20% intertriginous tier under DC 7829 Chloracne. Explicit applicability rule (83 FR 32592): claims pending prior to Aug. 13, 2018 are evaluated under both old and new criteria (whichever is more favorable); applications filed on/after Aug. 13, 2018 are governed solely by the new criteria.

versions.verbatimMarkdown:
**§ 4.118 Schedule of ratings—skin.**

**(a)** For the purposes of this section, systemic therapy is treatment that is administered through any route (orally, injection, suppository, intranasally) other than the skin, and topical therapy is treatment that is administered through the skin.

**(b)** Two or more skin conditions may be combined in accordance with § 4.25 only if separate areas of skin are involved. If two or more skin conditions involve the same area of skin, then only the highest evaluation shall be used.

**General Rating Formula For The Skin For DCs 7806, 7809, 7813–7816, 7820–7822, and 7824:**

* At least one of the following — **60**
  * Characteristic lesions involving more than 40 percent of the entire body or more than 40 percent of exposed areas affected; or
  * Constant or near-constant systemic therapy including, but not limited to, corticosteroids, phototherapy, retinoids, biologics, photochemotherapy, psoralen with long-wave ultraviolet-A light (PUVA), or other immunosuppressive drugs required over the past 12-month period.
* At least one of the following — **30**
  * Characteristic lesions involving 20 to 40 percent of the entire body or 20 to 40 percent of exposed areas affected; or
  * Systemic therapy including, but not limited to, corticosteroids, phototherapy, retinoids, biologics, photochemotherapy, PUVA, or other immunosuppressive drugs required for a total duration of 6 weeks or more, but not constantly, over the past 12-month period.
* At least one of the following — **10**
  * Characteristic lesions involving at least 5 percent, but less than 20 percent, of the entire body affected; or
  * At least 5 percent, but less than 20 percent, of exposed areas affected; or
  * Intermittent systemic therapy including, but not limited to, corticosteroids, phototherapy, retinoids, biologics, photochemotherapy, PUVA, or other immunosuppressive drugs required for a total duration of less than 6 weeks over the past 12-month period.
* No more than topical therapy required over the past 12-month period and at least one of the following — **0**
  * Characteristic lesions involving less than 5 percent of the entire body affected; or
  * Characteristic lesions involving less than 5 percent of exposed areas affected.
* Or rate as disfigurement of the head, face, or neck (DC 7800) or scars (DCs 7801, 7802, 7804, or 7805), depending upon the predominant disability. This rating instruction does not apply to DC 7824.

**7807 American (New World) leishmaniasis (mucocutaneous, espundia):**
Rate as disfigurement of the head, face, or neck (DC 7800), scars (DC's 7801, 7802, 7803, 7804, or 7805), or dermatitis (DC 7806), depending upon the predominant disability.
* **Note:** Evaluate non-cutaneous (visceral) leishmaniasis under DC 6301 (visceral leishmaniasis).

**7808 Old World leishmaniasis (cutaneous, Oriental sore):**
Rate as disfigurement of the head, face, or neck (DC 7800), scars (DC's, 7801, 7802, 7803, 7804, or 7805), or dermatitis (DC 7806), depending upon the predominant disability.
* **Note:** Evaluate non-cutaneous (visceral) leishmaniasis under DC 6301 (visceral leishmaniasis).

**7811 Tuberculosis luposa (lupus vulgaris), active or inactive:**
Rate under §§ 4.88c or 4.89, whichever is appropriate.

**7817 Erythroderma:**
* Generalized involvement of the skin with systemic manifestations (such as fever, weight loss, or hypoproteinemia) AND one of the following — **100**
  * Constant or near-constant systemic therapy such as therapeutic doses of corticosteroids, other immunosuppressive drugs, retinoids, PUVA (psoralen with long-wave ultraviolet-A light), UVB (ultraviolet-B light) treatments, biologics, or electron beam therapy required over the past 12-month period; or
  * No current treatment due to a documented history of treatment failure with 2 or more treatment regimens.
* Generalized involvement of the skin without systemic manifestations and one of the following — **60**
  * Constant or near-constant systemic therapy such as therapeutic doses of corticosteroids, other immunosuppressive drugs, retinoids, PUVA, UVB treatments, biologics, or electron beam therapy required over the past 12-month period; or
  * No current treatment due to a documented history of treatment failure with 1 treatment regimen.
* Any extent of involvement of the skin, and any of the following therapies required for a total duration of 6 weeks or more, but not constantly, over the past 12-month period: systemic therapy such as therapeutic doses of corticosteroids, other immunosuppressive drugs, retinoids, PUVA, UVB treatments, biologics, or electron beam therapy — **30**
* Any extent of involvement of the skin, and any of the following therapies required for a total duration of less than 6 weeks over the past 12-month period: systemic therapy such as therapeutic doses of corticosteroids, other immunosuppressive drugs, retinoids, PUVA, UVB treatments, biologics, or electron beam therapy — **10**
* Any extent of involvement of the skin, and no more than topical therapy required over the past 12-month period — **0**

**7818 Malignant skin neoplasms (other than malignant melanoma):**
Rate as disfigurement of the head, face, or neck (DC 7800), scars (DC's 7801, 7802, 7803, 7804, or 7805), or impairment of function.
* **Note:** If a skin malignancy requires therapy that is comparable to that used for systemic malignancies, i.e., systemic chemotherapy, X-ray therapy more extensive than to the skin, or surgery more extensive than wide local excision, a 100-percent evaluation will be assigned from the date of onset of treatment, and will continue, with a mandatory VA examination six months following the completion of such antineoplastic treatment, and any change in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination will be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter. If there has been no local recurrence or metastasis, evaluation will then be made on residuals. If treatment is confined to the skin, the provisions for a 100-percent evaluation do not apply.

**7819 Benign skin neoplasms:**
Rate as disfigurement of the head, face, or neck (DC 7800), scars (DC's 7801, 7802, 7803, 7804, or 7805), or impairment of function.

**7823 Vitiligo:**
* With exposed areas affected — **10**
* With no exposed areas affected — **0**

**7825 Chronic urticaria:**
For the purposes of this diagnostic code, chronic urticaria is defined as continuous urticaria at least twice per week, off treatment, for a period of six weeks or more.
* Chronic refractory urticaria that requires third line treatment for control (e.g., plasmapheresis, immunotherapy, immunosuppressives) due to ineffectiveness with first and second line treatments — **60**
* Chronic urticaria that requires second line treatment (e.g., corticosteroids, sympathomimetics, leukotriene inhibitors, neutrophil inhibitors, thyroid hormone) for control — **30**
* Chronic urticaria that requires first line treatment (antihistamines) for control — **10**

**7826 Vasculitis, primary cutaneous:**
* Persistent documented vasculitis episodes refractory to continuous immunosuppressive therapy — **60**
* All of the following — **30**
  * Recurrent documented vasculitic episodes occurring four or more times over the past 12-month period; and
  * Requiring intermittent systemic immunosuppressive therapy for control.
* At least one of the following — **10**
  * Recurrent documented vasculitic episodes occurring one to three times over the past 12-month period, and requiring intermittent systemic immunosuppressive therapy for control; or
  * Without recurrent documented vasculitic episodes but requiring continuous systemic medication for control.
* Or rate as disfigurement of the head, face, or neck (DC 7800) or scars (DCs 7801, 7802, 7804, or 7805), depending upon the predominant disability.

**7827 Erythema multiforme; Toxic epidermal necrolysis:**
* Recurrent mucosal, palmar, or plantar involvement impairing mastication, use of hands, or ambulation occurring four or more times over the past 12-month period despite ongoing immunosuppressive therapy — **60**
* All of the following — **30**
  * Recurrent mucosal, palmar, or plantar involvement not impairing mastication, use of hands, or ambulation, occurring four or more times over the past 12-month period; and
  * Requiring intermittent systemic therapy.
* At least one of the following — **10**
  * One to three episodes of mucosal, palmar, or plantar involvement not impairing mastication, use of hands, or ambulation, occurring over the past 12-month period and requiring intermittent systemic therapy; or
  * Without recurrent episodes, but requiring continuous systemic medication for control.
* Or rate as disfigurement of the head, face, or neck (DC 7800) or scars (DCs 7801, 7802, 7804, or 7805), depending upon the predominant disability.

**7828 Acne:**
* Deep acne (deep inflamed nodules and pus-filled cysts) affecting 40 percent or more of the face and neck — **30**
* Deep acne (deep inflamed nodules and pus-filled cysts) affecting less than 40 percent of the face and neck, or deep acne other than on the face and neck — **10**
* Superficial acne (comedones, papules, pustules) of any extent — **0**
* Or rate as disfigurement of the head, face, or neck (DC 7800) or scars (DCs 7801, 7802, 7804, or 7805), depending upon the predominant disability.

**7829 Chloracne:**
* Deep acne (deep inflamed nodules and pus-filled cysts) affecting 40 percent or more of the face and neck — **30**
* Deep acne (deep inflamed nodules and pus-filled cysts) affecting the intertriginous areas (the axilla of the arm, the anogenital region, skin folds of the breasts, or between digits) — **20**
* Deep acne (deep inflamed nodules and pus-filled cysts) affecting less than 40 percent of the face and neck; or deep acne affecting non-intertriginous areas of the body (other than the face and neck) — **10**
* Superficial acne (comedones, papules, pustules) of any extent — **0**
* Or rate as disfigurement of the head, face, or neck (DC 7800) or scars (DCs 7801, 7802, 7804, or 7805), depending upon the predominant disability.

**7830 Scarring alopecia:**
* Affecting more than 40 percent of the scalp — **20**
* Affecting 20 to 40 percent of the scalp — **10**
* Affecting less than 20 percent of the scalp — **0**

**7831 Alopecia areata:**
* With loss of all body hair — **10**
* With loss of hair limited to scalp and face — **0**

**7832 Hyperhidrosis:**
* Unable to handle paper or tools because of moisture, and unresponsive to therapy — **30**
* Able to handle paper or tools after therapy — **0**

**7833 Malignant melanoma:**
Rate as scars (DC's 7801, 7802, 7803, 7804, or 7805), disfigurement of the head, face, or neck (DC 7800), or impairment of function (under the appropriate body system).
* **Note:** If a skin malignancy requires therapy that is comparable to that used for systemic malignancies, i.e., systemic chemotherapy, X-ray therapy more extensive than to the skin, or surgery more extensive than wide local excision, a 100-percent evaluation will be assigned from the date of onset of treatment, and will continue, with a mandatory VA examination six months following the completion of such antineoplastic treatment, and any change in evaluation based upon that or any subsequent examination will be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter. If there has been no local recurrence or metastasis, evaluation will then be made on residuals. If treatment is confined to the skin, the provisions for a 100-percent evaluation do not apply.

trapTables.title: 1. Master Chronological Federal Register & Precedent Ledger (1946–2026)
rows: Established Era-1 qualitative skin schedules (DC 7806–7819): DC 7806 Eczema (50/30/10/0% ulceration, exfoliation, exudation, itching), DC 7816 Psoriasis (50/30/10/0%), DC 7817 Exfoliative dermatitis (100/50/30/0%), DC 7818 Malignant skin neoplasms, plus tropical/fungal codes (7807–7815).

CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (< Aug. 30, 2002): Governs pre-Aug. 30, 2002 CUE audits. Under Pernorio v. Derwinski, 2 Vet. App. 625 (1992), BVA could not invent extra-regulatory physical-excoriation requirements to prove itching.

First Major Skin Overhaul (Era 2): Replaced qualitative Era-1 tiers with 60 / 30 / 10 / 0% Body Surface Area (BSA) / Exposed-Area % OR "systemic therapy such as corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive drugs" (12-month duration); removed obsolete DC 7810 (Pinta), DC 7812 (Verruga peruana), and DC 7814 (Tinea barbae); enacted DC 7820–7833 (infections, collagen-vascular, vitiligo, urticaria, vasculitis, acne, chloracne, alopecia, hyperhidrosis, malignant melanoma).

CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (Aug. 30, 2002 – Aug. 12, 2018): Assigning 10% when DBQ documented 20–40% exposed-area involvement (= 30%) or >=6 weeks oral prednisone/methotrexate (= 30%) is plain-text CUE.
73 FR 54708 (pub. Sept. 23, 2008; clarified 77 FR 2909, Jan. 20, 2012)

Overhauled DC 7800–7805 Scars & Head/Face/Neck Disfigurement (8-characteristic matrix + DC 7804 painful/unstable scar count; removed DC 7803 — see Scars Diff). Cross-impacts DC 7807–7808, 7818–7819, 7828–7829, and 7833 residual scar evaluations!
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (>= Oct. 23, 2008) on scar/disfigurement residuals.
Warren v. McDonald, 28 Vet. App. 194 (2016) & Johnson v. Shulkin, 862 F.3d 1351 (Fed. Cir. 2017)

Warren held "such as" in Era-2 DC 7806 is illustrative, encompassing any systemic therapy akin to corticosteroids/immunosuppressives; Johnson v. Shulkin (rev'g 27 Vet. App. 497) held localized topical corticosteroid cream is topical rather than systemic therapy unless applied on so widespread a scale that it acts systemically.
Warren is Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) on CUE against final pre-2016 decisions; Johnson v. Shulkin enforces the plain boundary barring topical-cream CUE claims.

Second Major Skin Overhaul (Era 3 — Current Law): Codified § 4.118(a) route-of-administration definitions of systemic vs. topical therapy (explicitly adding biologics, retinoids, phototherapy, photochemotherapy, PUVA); unified General Rating Formula for the Skin across 9 DCs (7806, 7809, 7813, 7815–7816, 7820–7822, 7824); rewrote DC 7817 Erythroderma (100/60/30/10/0%), DC 7825 Urticaria (1st/2nd/3rd-line therapy), DC 7826–7827, and reduced superficial DC 7828/7829 acne/chloracne from 10% to 0%.

CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (>= Aug. 13, 2018): Assigning < 60% when a veteran requires constant/near-constant systemic biologic therapy (Dupixent, Humira, Skyrizi, Cosentyx, Otezla) over 12 months is plain-text CUE! Pre-Aug. 13, 2018 awards are protected under 38 U.S.C. § 1155.

Added somatic "melanoma of the skin" (DC 7833) and neck cancers (DC 7818/7833) as PACT Act burn-pit presumptions, and eliminated § 1117 Gulf War 10% threshold & sunset for undiagnosed skin rashes (Playbook 15).
Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (>= Aug. 10, 2022) + 38 U.S.C. § 1305 / § 3.33 retroactive survivor DIC re-evaluations.
Sept. 29, 2025 (Proposed Only)
QUARANTINED — Proposed / Not Finalized: Proposed adding a note to DC 7804 requiring objective exam demonstration of scar pain.
ZERO legal force (see Section 5).

trapTables.title: 2. Three-Era Evolution of Dermatitis, Eczema, Psoriasis & The General Rating Formula (DC 7806, 7809, 7813, 7815–7816, 7820–7822, 7824)
headers: Era 3: Aug. 13, 2018 – Present (83 FR 32592 Unified General Rating Formula for the Skin)
rows: Covered DCs
Separate bespoke schedules under DC 7806 (Eczema), DC 7809 (30/10%), DC 7813 (30/10/0%), DC 7815 (60/30/10%), and DC 7816 (Psoriasis).
Shared DC 7806 template referenced by DC 7809, 7813, 7815, 7816, 7820, 7821, 7822, 7824 (Note: DC 7814 Tinea barbae was removed Aug. 30, 2002).
Unified General Rating Formula for the Skin directly governing 9 codes: DC 7806, 7809, 7813, 7815, 7816, 7820, 7821, 7822, and 7824.

• DC 7806 (50%): Ulceration or extensive exfoliation or crusting, and systemic or nervous manifestations, or exceptionally repugnant. · • DC 7816 (50%): Generalized, with severe involvement of hands/feet or severe constitutional manifestations (Note: DC 7815 Pemphigus topped at 60%).

More than 40% of the entire body OR more than 40% of exposed areas affected, OR; constant or near-constant systemic therapy such as corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive drugs required during the past 12-month period.

At least one of the following: · • Characteristic lesions involving more than 40% of the entire body OR more than 40% of exposed areas affected; OR · • Constant or near-constant systemic therapy including, but not limited to, corticosteroids, phototherapy, retinoids, biologics, photochemotherapy, psoralen with long-wave ultraviolet-A light (PUVA), or other immunosuppressive drugs required over the past 12-month period.

• DC 7806 (30%): Exudation or constant itching, or extensive lesions, or marked disfigurement (Pernorio: no physical excoriation required to prove constant itching!). · • DC 7816 (30%): Moderately extensive (>10% BSA) or chronic lesions of exposed parts.

20% to 40% of the entire body OR 20% to 40% of exposed areas affected, OR; systemic therapy such as corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive drugs required for a total duration of 6 weeks or more, but not constantly, during the past 12-month period.

At least one of the following: · • Characteristic lesions involving 20% to 40% of the entire body OR 20% to 40% of exposed areas affected; OR · • Systemic therapy (corticosteroids, phototherapy, retinoids, biologics, photochemotherapy, PUVA, or other immunosuppressive drugs) required for a total duration of 6 weeks or more, but not constantly, over the past 12-month period.
• DC 7806 (10%): Slight, dry, scaly, with intermittent itching. · • DC 7816 (10%): Scattered, sparse plaques.

At least 5%, but less than 20% of the entire body, OR at least 5%, but less than 20% of exposed areas affected, OR; intermittent systemic therapy such as corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive drugs required for a total duration of less than 6 weeks during the past 12-month period.

At least one of the following: · • Characteristic lesions involving 5% to 19% of the entire body OR 5% to 19% of exposed areas affected; OR · • Systemic therapy required for a total duration of less than 6 weeks over the past 12-month period.
Slight, infrequent, or healed without disfiguring residuals.
Less than 5% of the entire body and less than 5% of exposed areas affected, AND; no more than topical therapy required during the past 12-month period.

At least one of the following (where higher tiers are not met): · • Characteristic lesions involving less than 5% of the entire body and less than 5% of exposed areas affected; and/or · • No more than topical therapy required over the past 12-month period.
