**§ 4.85 Evaluation of hearing impairment.**

**(a)** An examination for hearing impairment for VA purposes must be conducted by a state-licensed audiologist and must include a controlled speech discrimination test (Maryland CNC) and a puretone audiometry test. Examinations will be conducted without the use of hearing aids.

**(b)** Table VI, “Numeric Designation of Hearing Impairment Based on Puretone Threshold Average and Speech Discrimination,” is used to determine a Roman numeral designation (I through XI) for hearing impairment based on a combination of the percent of speech discrimination (horizontal rows) and the puretone threshold average (vertical columns). The Roman numeral designation is located at the point where the percentage of speech discrimination and puretone threshold average intersect.

**(c)** Table VIa, “Numeric Designation of Hearing Impairment Based Only on Puretone Threshold Average,” is used to determine a Roman numeral designation (I through XI) for hearing impairment based only on the puretone threshold average. Table VIa will be used when the examiner certifies that use of the speech discrimination test is not appropriate because of language difficulties, inconsistent speech discrimination scores, etc., or when indicated under the provisions of § 4.86.

**(d)** “Puretone threshold average,” as used in Tables VI and VIa, is the sum of the puretone thresholds at 1000, 2000, 3000 and 4000 Hertz, divided by four. This average is used in all cases (including those in § 4.86) to determine the Roman numeral designation for hearing impairment from Table VI or VIa.

**(e)** Table VII, “Percentage Evaluations for Hearing Impairment,” is used to determine the percentage evaluation by combining the Roman numeral designations for hearing impairment of each ear. The horizontal rows represent the ear having the better hearing and the vertical columns the ear having the poorer hearing. The percentage evaluation is located at the point where the row and column intersect.

**(f)** If impaired hearing is service-connected in only one ear, in order to determine the percentage evaluation from Table VII, the non-service-connected ear will be assigned a Roman Numeral designation for hearing impairment of I, subject to the provisions of § 3.383 of this chapter.

**(g)** When evaluating any claim for impaired hearing, refer to § 3.350 of this chapter to determine whether the veteran may be entitled to special monthly compensation due either to deafness, or to deafness in combination with other specified disabilities.

**(h)** Numeric tables VI, VIA*, and VII.

**§ 4.86 Exceptional patterns of hearing impairment.**

**(a)** When the puretone threshold at each of the four specified frequencies (1000, 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hertz) is 55 decibels or more, the rating specialist will determine the Roman numeral designation for hearing impairment from either Table VI or Table VIa, whichever results in the higher numeral. Each ear will be evaluated separately.

**(b)** When the puretone threshold is 30 decibels or less at 1000 Hertz, and 70 decibels or more at 2000 Hertz, the rating specialist will determine the Roman numeral designation for hearing impairment from either Table VI or Table VIa, whichever results in the higher numeral. That numeral will then be elevated to the next higher Roman numeral. Each ear will be evaluated separately.

*(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 1155)*

**§ 4.87 Schedule of ratings—ear.**

**Diseases of the Ear**

* **6200 Chronic suppurative otitis media, mastoiditis, or cholesteatoma (or any combination):**
  * During suppuration, or with aural polyps — **10**
  * *Note:* Evaluate hearing impairment, and complications such as labyrinthitis, tinnitus, facial nerve paralysis, or bone loss of skull, separately.
* **6201 Chronic nonsuppurative otitis media with effusion (serous otitis media):** Rate hearing impairment.
* **6202 Otosclerosis:** Rate hearing impairment.
* **6204 Peripheral vestibular disorders:**
  * Dizziness and occasional staggering — **30**
  * Occasional dizziness — **10**
  * *Note:* Objective findings supporting the diagnosis of vestibular disequilibrium are required before a compensable evaluation can be assigned under this code. Hearing impairment or suppuration shall be separately rated and combined.
* **6205 Meniere's syndrome (endolymphatic hydrops):**
  * Hearing impairment with attacks of vertigo and cerebellar gait occurring more than once weekly, with or without tinnitus — **100**
  * Hearing impairment with attacks of vertigo and cerebellar gait occurring from one to four times a month, with or without tinnitus — **60**
  * Hearing impairment with vertigo less than once a month, with or without tinnitus — **30**
  * *Note:* Evaluate Meniere's syndrome either under these criteria or by separately evaluating vertigo (as a peripheral vestibular disorder), hearing impairment, and tinnitus, whichever method results in a higher overall evaluation. But do not combine an evaluation for hearing impairment, tinnitus, or vertigo with an evaluation under diagnostic code 6205.
* **6207 Loss of auricle:**
  * Complete loss of both ¹ — **50**
  * Complete loss of one — **30**
  * Deformity of one, with loss of one-third or more of the substance — **10**
* **6208 Malignant neoplasm of the ear (other than skin only)** — **100**
  * *Note:* A rating of 100 percent shall continue beyond the cessation of any surgical, radiation treatment, antineoplastic chemotherapy or other therapeutic procedure. Six months after discontinuance of such treatment, the appropriate disability rating shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any change in evaluation based on that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter. If there has been no local recurrence or metastasis, rate on residuals.
* **6209 Benign neoplasms of the ear (other than skin only):** Rate on impairment of function.
* **6210 Chronic otitis externa:**
  * Swelling, dry and scaly or serous discharge, and itching requiring frequent and prolonged treatment — **10**
* **6211 Tympanic membrane, perforation of** — **0**

¹ Review for entitlement to special monthly compensation under § 3.350 of this chapter.

rows: 1945 VASRD (38 C.F.R. § 3.952; 29 FR 6718, May 22, 1964; 41 FR 11298, Mar. 18, 1976 ISO/ANSI puretone tables)

Era 1 Spoken-Voice / Early Audiometric Schedule: Evaluated auditory acuity initially by conversational voice distance (1/3/5/10/15/20 ft, Columns A–F) and later early puretone + PB word lists (DC 6277–6297); DC 6260 Tinnitus required "Persistent as a symptom of head injury, concussion or acoustic trauma — 10%".

CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (< Dec. 18, 1987): Governs pre-Dec. 18, 1987 hearing loss CUE audits; running pre-Dec. 18, 1987 awards protected from schedule-change reduction under 38 U.S.C. § 1155 / § 3.951(a).

Modern Audiometric Overhaul (§ 4.85, DC 6100): Replaced spoken-voice/legacy DC 6277–6297 codes with un-aided state-licensed audiologist testing combining 1000–4000 Hz Puretone Threshold Average (PTA) + Maryland CNC Speech Discrimination (Tables VI, VIa & VII, Roman Numerals I–XI -> 0%–100% under unified DC 6100).
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (>= Dec. 18, 1987): Mechanical math errors reading Table VI, Table VIa, or Table VII on undisputed audiograms are textbook RO CUE (§ 3.105(a)).

Enacted and refined 38 C.F.R. § 3.385 (Disability due to impaired hearing): >= 40 dB at any of 500–4000 Hz, OR >= 26 dB at >= 3 of 500–4000 Hz, OR < 94% Maryland CNC speech recognition (59 FR 60560 added the < 94% CNC prong).
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive: Under Hensley v. Brown, 5 Vet. App. 155 (1993), § 3.385 governs current disability—never a bar requiring § 3.385-level loss on a separation audiogram!

Under 32-97 & Boyer, unilateral SC hearing loss fixes the NSC ear at Roman Numeral I unless 38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(3) / § 3.383(a)(3) applies: pre-Dec. 6, 2002 required total deafness in both ears; on/after Dec. 6, 2002, Pub. L. 107-330, § 103 liberalized § 1160(a)(3) to >= 10% compensable SC hearing loss in one ear (Roman Numeral X or XI) + § 3.385 NSC hearing loss in the other ear!

Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) / CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (>= Dec. 6, 2002): Huge CUE/effective-date unlock whenever a post-Dec. 6, 2002 10%+ unilateral SC ear was not combined with a § 3.385 NSC ear!

Overhauled §§ 4.85–4.87a: Enacted § 4.86(a)–(b) Exceptional Patterns of Hearing Impairment (>= 55 dB at 1000–4000 Hz, OR <= 30 dB at 1000 Hz & >= 70 dB at 2000 Hz); liberalized DC 6260 Tinnitus to "Tinnitus, recurrent — 10%" (deleting the head-injury/concussion/acoustic-trauma limitation + adding Notes (1) & (2) [redesignated Note (3) in 2003]); codified DC 6205 Meniere's 30/60/100% + anti-pyramiding maximization Note; separated DC 6275–6276 smell/taste into § 4.87a.

CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (>= June 10, 1999): Rater failure to apply § 4.86(a) or (b) on post-June 10, 1999 audiograms is one of the highest-yield math CUEs in Veterans Law! Zero CUE reach before June 10, 1999.
VAOPGCPREC 2-2003 (69 FR 25178); 68 FR 25822 (pub. May 14, 2003, RIN 2900-AK86); Smith v. Nicholson, 451 F.3d 1344 (Fed. Cir. 2006)

Adverse CUE Kill-Switch: Defeats all bilateral 10% + 10% tinnitus claims and CUE motions regardless of decision date.

(Satisfied by Romberg sway, nystagmus, Dix-Hallpike, VNG/ENG caloric testing, or observed gait unsteadiness!). Combine DC 6100, DC 6200, and DC 6260 separately!
Meniere's syndrome (endolymphatic hydrops)

• 100%: Hearing impairment with attacks of vertigo and cerebellar gait occurring more than once weekly (> 1/wk), with or without tinnitus. · • 60%: Hearing impairment with attacks of vertigo and cerebellar gait occurring 1 to 4 times a month, with or without tinnitus. · • 30%: Hearing impairment with vertigo less than once a month (< 1/mo), with or without tinnitus. · • CRITICAL MAXIMIZATION & ANTI-PYRAMIDING NOTE (38 C.F.R. § 4.14; DC 6205 Note, 64 FR 25202, 25210): Evaluate Meniere's EITHER as a single DC 6205 rating (30/60/100%) OR by separately rating vertigo (DC 6204, 10%/30%), hearing loss (DC 6100, 0%–100%), and tinnitus (DC 6260, 10%) and combining them under § 4.25—WHICHEVER METHOD YIELDS THE HIGHER OVERALL EVALUATION! title: Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers (PCAFC Current Text Through Sept. 30, 2028 Extension)
summary: CRITICAL ARCHIVAL CFR-PART DISAMBIGUATION: 38 C.F.R. §§ 17.4000–17.4040 (84 FR 26278, pub. June 5, 2019, eff. June 6, 2019) codifies the 38 U.S.C. § 1703 Veterans Community Care Program (including the § 17.4020(c)(2) 72-hour emergency-treatment notification rule), whereas the VA MISSION Act PCAFC overhaul (38 U.S.C. § 1720G) published July 31, 2020 at 85 FR 46226, 46293 and effective October 1, 2020 is codified in 38 C.F.R. Part 71 (§§ 71.10–71.50): enacted the >=70% 'serious injury' definition (§ 71.15), two-phase pre-May 7, 1975 (Oct. 1, 2020) and post-May 7, 1975–Sept. 10, 2001 (Oct. 1, 2022, 86 FR 52614) era expansion (§ 71.20(a)(2)), OPM GS-4 Step 1 locality monthly stipend tiers at 62.5% vs. 100% 'unable to self-sustain in the community' (§ 71.40(c)(4)(i)(A)), 60-day advance revocation/discharge notices (§ 71.45), and 8-year legacy cohort eligibility extended through September 30, 2028 (90 FR 46477, pub. Sept. 29, 2025, eff. Sept. 30, 2025). Partially invalidated in Veteran Warriors, Inc. v. Sec'y of Veterans Affairs, 29 F.4th 1320 (Fed. Cir. 2022), and held reviewable before the Board and CAVC notwithstanding 38 U.S.C. § 1720G(c)(1) / 38 C.F.R. § 20.104(c) in Beaudette v. McDonough, 93 F.4th 1361 (Fed. Cir. 2024). QUARANTINE NOTE: Proposed PCAFC rule 89 FR 97404 (Dec. 6, 2024, RIN 2900-AR96) remains proposed / not finalized.

**§ 71.15 Definitions.**

[...]

**In need of personal care services** means that the eligible veteran requires in-person personal care services from another person, and without such personal care services, alternative in-person caregiving arrangements (including respite care or assistance of an alternative caregiver) would be required to support the eligible veteran's safety.

**Monthly stipend rate** means the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) General Schedule (GS) Annual Rate for grade 4, step 1, based on the locality pay area in which the eligible veteran resides, divided by 12.

**Need for supervision, protection, or instruction** means an individual has a functional impairment that directly impacts the individual's ability to maintain his or her personal safety on a daily basis.

**Serious injury** means any service-connected disability that:
* **(1)** Is rated at 70 percent or more by VA; or
* **(2)** Is combined with any other service-connected disability or disabilities, and a combined rating of 70 percent or more is assigned by VA.

**Unable to self-sustain in the community** means that an eligible veteran:
* **(1)** Requires personal care services each time he or she completes three or more of the seven activities of daily living (ADL) listed in the definition of an inability to perform an activity of daily living in this section, and is fully dependent on a caregiver to complete such ADLs; or
* **(2)** Has a need for supervision, protection, or instruction on a continuous basis.

**§ 71.20 Eligible veterans and servicemembers.**

A veteran or servicemember is eligible for a Family Caregiver under this part if he or she meets the criteria in paragraph (a), (b), or (c) of this section, subject to the limitations set forth in such paragraphs.

**(a)** A veteran or servicemember is eligible for a Primary or Secondary Family Caregiver under this part if he or she meets all of the following requirements:
* **(1)** The individual is either:
  * **(i)** A veteran; or
  * **(ii)** A member of the Armed Forces undergoing a medical discharge from the Armed Forces.
* **(2)** The individual has a serious injury incurred or aggravated in the line of duty in the active military, naval, or air service:
  * **(i)** On or after September 11, 2001;
  * **(ii)** Effective October 1, 2020, on or before May 7, 1975; or
  * **(iii)** Effective October 1, 2022, after May 7, 1975 and before September 11, 2001.
* **(3)** The individual is in need of personal care services for a minimum of six continuous months based on any one of the following:
  * **(i)** An inability to perform an activity of daily living; or
  * **(ii)** A need for supervision, protection, or instruction.
* **(4)** It is in the best interest of the individual to participate in the program.
* **(5)** Personal care services that would be provided by the Family Caregiver will not be simultaneously and regularly provided by or through another individual or entity.
* **(6)** The individual receives care at home or will do so if VA designates a Family Caregiver.
* **(7)** The individual receives ongoing care from a primary care team or will do so if VA designates a Family Caregiver.

**(b)** For eight years beginning on October 1, 2020, a veteran or servicemember is eligible for a Primary or Secondary Family Caregiver under this part if he or she is a legacy participant.

**(c)** For eight years beginning on October 1, 2020, a veteran or servicemember is eligible for a Primary or Secondary Family Caregiver under this part if he or she is a legacy applicant. *(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 501, 1720G(a)(2))*

**§ 71.25 Approval and designation of Primary and Secondary Family Caregivers.**

**(a) Application requirement.**
* **(1)** Individuals who wish to be considered for designation by VA as Primary or Secondary Family Caregivers must submit a joint application, along with the veteran or servicemember. Individuals interested in serving as Family Caregivers must be identified as such on the joint application, and no more than three individuals may serve as Family Caregivers at one time for an eligible veteran, with no more than one serving as the Primary Family Caregiver and no more than two serving as Secondary Family Caregivers.

[...]

**(b) Eligibility to serve as Primary or Secondary Family Caregiver.** In order to serve as a Primary or Secondary Family Caregiver, the applicant must meet all of the following requirements:
* **(1)** Be at least 18 years of age.
* **(2)** Be either:
  * **(i)** The eligible veteran's spouse, son, daughter, parent, step-family member, or extended family member; or
  * **(ii)** Someone who lives with the eligible veteran full-time or will do so if designated as a Family Caregiver.
* **(3)** There must be no determination by VA of abuse or neglect of the eligible veteran by the applicant.
* **(4)** Meet the requirements of paragraph (c) of this section, and any other applicable requirements of this part.

**§ 71.40 Caregiver benefits.**

[...]

**(c) Primary Family Caregiver benefits.** VA will provide to Primary Family Caregivers all of the benefits listed in paragraphs (c)(1) through (4) of this section.
* [...]
* **(4) Monthly stipend.** Primary Family Caregivers are eligible to receive a monthly stipend, calculated for each eligible veteran in accordance with this paragraph (c)(4).
  * **(i) Stipend amount.**
    * **(A)** Except as provided in paragraph (c)(4)(i)(B) of this section:
      * **(1)** The Primary Family Caregiver's monthly stipend is calculated by multiplying the monthly stipend rate by 0.625.
      * **(2)** If VA determines that the eligible veteran is unable to self-sustain in the community, the Primary Family Caregiver's monthly stipend is calculated by multiplying the monthly stipend rate by 1.00.

**§ 71.45 Revocation and discharge of Family Caregivers.**

**(a) Revocation of the Family Caregiver**—
* [...]
* **(1)(ii) Noncompliance.** [...]
  * **(iii)** In the case of revocation based on noncompliance under paragraph (a)(1)(ii) of this section, revocation takes effect as of the effective date provided in VA's final notice of such revocation to the eligible veteran and Family Caregiver. The effective date of revocation will be no earlier than 60 days after VA provides advanced notice of its findings to the eligible veteran and Family Caregiver.

**(b) Discharge of the Family Caregiver**—
* **(1) Discharge due to the eligible veteran.** [...]
  * **(ii)(A)** In the case of discharge based on paragraph (b)(1)(i)(A) of this section, the discharge takes effect as of the effective date provided in VA's final notice of such discharge to the eligible veteran and Family Caregiver. The effective date of discharge will be no earlier than 60 days after VA provides advanced notice of its findings to the eligible veteran and Family Caregiver that the eligible veteran does not meet the requirements of § 71.20.

**§ 20.104 Rule 104. Jurisdiction of the Board.**

[...]

**(c) Medical determinations.** Medical determinations, such as determinations of the need for and appropriateness of specific types of medical care and treatment for an individual, are not adjudicative matters and are beyond the Board's jurisdiction. Typical examples of these issues are whether a particular drug should be prescribed, whether a specific type of physiotherapy should be ordered, and similar judgmental treatment decisions with which an attending physician may be faced. *(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 511(a), 7104)*

title: Compensation for certain disabilities occurring in Persian Gulf veterans

title: Benefits under 38 U.S.C. 1151(a) for additional disability or death due to hospital care, medical or surgical treatment, examination, training and rehabilitation services, or compensated work therapy program
summary: Published August 3, 2004, regulatory effective date September 2, 2004 (RIN 2900-AJ42), implementing Pub. L. 104-204, § 422 (110 Stat. 2874, 2926) which statutorily abrogated Brown v. Gardner, 513 U.S. 115 (1994) for claims received on or after October 1, 1997 (note: Pub. L. 104-204, § 422(b)(2) originally set Jan. 1, 1997, delayed to Oct. 1, 1997 by Pub. L. 104-275, § 602(b)). Preserves no-fault § 3.358 strictly for claims received before October 1, 1997 that remained continuously pending (not finally disallowed), while codifying §§ 3.361–3.363 for all original claims AND claims to reopen finally disallowed pre-1997 claims received on or after October 1, 1997 (§ 3.361(a)(1)–(2))—requiring proximate causation via carelessness, negligence, lack of proper skill, error in judgment, lack of informed consent (§ 3.361(d)(1)), or an 'event not reasonably foreseeable' (§ 3.361(d)(2); Viegas v. Shinseki, 705 F.3d 1374 (Fed. Cir. 2013)), plus FTCA tort judgment/settlement offset mechanics under § 3.362.

trapTables.title: Master Structural Index of 38 C.F.R. Part 4, Subpart A (§§ 4.1–4.31)
headers: Bitemporal CUE vs. Open-Claim Posture (George v. McDonough)
rows: Essentials of evaluative rating; Interpretation of examination reports; Evaluation of evidence
Requires evaluating current exams in light of the entire recorded medical & industrial history (Schafrath).

Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) on weighing disputes; CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive only if undisputed probative evidence in the record was completely ignored with outcome-determinative effect.
Resolution of reasonable doubt
Applies 38 U.S.C. § 5107(b) equipoise to the degree of disability within a Diagnostic Code (Bufkin).
Never CUE (38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(d)(3) — failure to give benefit of the doubt cannot constitute CUE); open-claim/appeal tool reviewed for clear error at CAVC (Bufkin).
Higher of two evaluations
Awards higher evaluation when disability picture "more nearly approximates" higher tier (Tatum vs. Camacho/Middleton).
Generally Open-Claim Only: Subjective "more nearly approximates" judgment calls cannot support CUE (Russell/Fugo), unless all objective criteria of the higher tier were undisputedly met.
Congenital or developmental defects
Excludes static structural defects, refractive error, personality disorder, and intellectual disability (mirrors § 3.303(c)).
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (>= July 18, 1990): Misclassifying a progressive hereditary disease as a noncompensable § 4.9/§ 3.303(c) defect violates VAOPGCPREC 82-90 (Causation Treatise).
Functional impairment
Anchors ratings to functional ability under ordinary conditions of life, including employment; bars uncodified medication discounting (Jones; Ingram).

Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) for pre-2025 final decisions under Ingram; immediate HLR/Supplemental/Appeal audit for ratings issued during the rescinded 91 FR 7118 IFR window (Feb. 17–27, 2026).
Effect of change of diagnosis
Separates progression of prior condition from correction of diagnostic error; protects prior SC (Read v. Shinseki).
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive if VA severed SC without § 3.105(d)/§ 3.957 compliance; diagnostic code reclassification preserving SC is not a severance (Read).
Avoidance of pyramiding
Bars compensating the exact same manifestation twice (Brady), while mandating separate ratings for distinct actual symptoms (Esteban; Morgan).

CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive when VA double-counted identical symptoms OR refused a mandatory separate rating (e.g., Spine Note 1 radiculopathy, VAOPGCPREC 23-97/9-2004 knee instability + flexion + extension) on undisputed C&P facts.
Total disability ratings; TDIU (§ 4.16); Pension (§ 4.17); Misconduct etiology (§ 4.17a); Unemployability (§ 4.18)
Governs constitutional/individual total impairment, § 4.16(a)–(b) TDIU, protected/static trauma employment termination (§ 4.18), and coexisting misconduct insulation (§ 4.17a).

CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive on § 4.16(a)(1)–(5) single-disability aggregation math errors; Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) on § 4.16(b) extraschedular referrals (TDIU Digestive Respiratory Diffs).
Age in service-connected claims
Strictly prohibits considering advancing age in evaluating SC disability compensation or TDIU (§ 4.16).
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive if a rating narrative explicitly discounted an SC evaluation or denied TDIU on the face of the decision due to the veteran's advanced age.
Analogous ratings (§ 4.20); Application of schedule (§ 4.21); Use of diagnostic code numbers (§ 4.27)
Three-factor analogy test (Lendenmann); no rigid literal-identity barrier (Webb); xx99-xxxx hyphenation (§ 4.27).
Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) for Webb (2023) and initial choice among competing plausible analogous codes.
Aggravation baseline deduction (§ 4.22); Attitude of rating officers (§ 4.23); Central Office correspondence (§ 4.24)
Deducts ascertainable entrance schedular % on § 1153 aggravation (zero deduction if 100% or unascertainable!).
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive when VA deducted an arbitrary/unascertainable entrance percentage or deducted from a 100% evaluation in violation of § 4.22.
Combined ratings table (§ 4.25); Bilateral factor (§ 4.26(a)–(d))
Whole-person efficiency (100 - remaining efficiency), .5 rounding, +10% paired-extremity bonus, and Apr. 16, 2023 § 4.26(d) exclusion (88 FR 22914).
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive for pure § 4.25 arithmetic/rounding errors, omitted mandatory § 4.26(a)–(c) bilateral bonus, or omitted § 4.26(d) exclusion on/after Apr. 16, 2023.
Prestabilization (§ 4.28); Hospitalization >21 days (§ 4.29); Convalescence (§ 4.30)
Mandatory temporary 50%/100% (§ 4.28) or 100% (§§ 4.29, 4.30) + Bradley statutory SMC(s).
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive when VAMC/surgical records in the record at adjudication undisputedly met objective >21-day hospital or cast/surgical criteria (or omitted >=2008 Bradley SMC(s)).
Zero percent evaluations
Mandatory 0% SC evaluation whenever a DC lacks an explicit 0% tier and compensable criteria are unmet.
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive if VA denied service connection outright solely because current symptoms did not reach a 10% compensable threshold!

trapTables.title: C. 38 C.F.R. § 4.7 (Higher of Two Evaluations): Disjunctive vs. Conjunctive vs. Successive/Cumulative Criteria
rows: 1. Successive / Cumulative Conjunctive Criteria ("and" cascading upward)
Camacho v. Nicholson, 21 Vet. App. 360, 366–67 (2007); Middleton v. Shinseki, 727 F.3d 1172, 1177–78 (Fed. Cir. 2013)

§ 4.7 CANNOT Bypass Missing Prongs: Where each ascending tier explicitly incorporates all requirements of the preceding lower tier plus an additional criterion joined by "and", the veteran must satisfy every cumulative prong. Failing a required lower-tier element (e.g., "regulation of activities") forecloses § 4.7 even if the veteran has the higher tier's extra symptom!

DC 7913 Diabetes Mellitus: 20% (insulin AND restricted diet) -> 40% (insulin, restricted diet, AND regulation of activities) -> 60% (40% criteria + episodes of ketoacidosis/hypoglycemic reactions). Under Middleton, ketoacidosis hospitalizations without regulation of activities cannot yield 40% or 60% via § 4.7!
2. Variable / Non-Successive Multi-Symptom Criteria
Tatum v. Shinseki, 23 Vet. App. 152, 156 (2009)

§ 4.7 FULLY APPLIES: Even when a tier lists multiple symptoms joined by "and", if the rating tiers are not structured as rigid upward-cascading cumulative steps, the Board must apply § 4.7 to decide whether the veteran's overall severity more nearly approximates the higher tier despite lacking one listed symptom!

Pre-2017 DC 7903 Hypothyroidism (Tatum: 10% vs. 30% tiers listed distinct symptom clusters rather than incorporating lower tiers verbatim, requiring a § 4.7 approximation analysis); Pre-May 2024 DC 7346 Hiatal Hernia/GERD (30% vs. 60%).
3. Exemplar / Holistic Occupational-Impairment Formulas ("such symptoms as" / "or")
Vazquez-Claudio v. Shinseki, 713 F.3d 112, 116–18 (Fed. Cir. 2013); Bankhead v. Shulkin, 29 Vet. App. 10, 21–23 (2017)

§ 4.7 & Symptom-Driven Holistic Assessment: Listed symptoms are non-exhaustive examples demonstrating the frequency, type, and severity of occupational/social impairment. Presence of a higher-tier hallmark symptom (e.g., passive suicidal ideation at 70% under Bankhead—requiring no plan, intent, or hospitalization!) compels rigorous § 4.7 analysis of overall impairment.

Effective day following separation (38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(1) when claimed within 1 year of discharge). Exclusion: Never assigned if the veteran immediately qualifies for an equal or higher regular schedular 100% evaluation (§ 4.28).

• 100% beginning on the first day of continuous SC hospitalization (§ 4.29(a)–(b)), with physician-approved temporary releases not breaking continuity (§ 4.29(a)). · • Terminates last day of the month of hospital discharge (or release to non-bed care) OR last day of the month of termination of SC treatment/observation (§ 4.29(a)), plus optional 1, 2, or 3 mos post-discharge convalescence (§ 4.29(e)) and 1, 2, or 3 further mos with VSCM approval (§ 4.29(f)).

Peake, 22 Vet. App. 280 (2008)).

Convalescent Ratings (100% Post-Surgical or Cast Immobilization) — Treatment in a VA or any hospital/outpatient surgical center for an SC disability resulting in: · (1) Surgery necessitating at least 1 month of convalescence (§ 4.30(a)(1)); · (2) Surgery with severe postoperative residuals (incompletely healed surgical wounds, therapeutic immobilizing casts, crutches/wheelchair inability to navigate, or strict house confinement) (§ 4.30(a)(2)); OR · (3) Immobilization by cast, without surgery, of one or more major joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee, ankle) (§ 4.30(a)(3)).

• 100% from date of hospital admission or outpatient surgery/cast application. · • Initial Duration: 1, 2, or 3 months from the first day of the month following hospital discharge or outpatient release (§ 4.30). · • Extensions: Extendable by 1, 2, or 3 additional months (up to 6 mos total) under (a)(1)–(3) (§ 4.30(b)(1)), and 1 to 6 further months (up to 12 mos total) under (a)(2)–(3) with VSCM approval (§ 4.30(b)(2)).

Cir. 2016) & 85 FR 76453): Under Hudgens, partial knee replacements qualified under pre-Feb. 7, 2021 DC 5055 (1-year 100%) for claims filed/pending before VA's interim rule (80 FR 42040, July 16, 2015); effective Feb. 7, 2021 (85 FR 76453), total joint replacements (DC 5054/5055) carry a 4-month 100% period while partial/resurfacing procedures fall under § 4.30. · • § 3.105(e) Reduction Trap: Expiring a fixed § 4.30 period back to the pre-surgical running baseline is exempt from § 3.105(e) (§ 4.30 text), HOWEVER, reducing a veteran below their pre-surgical baseline evaluation—or discontinuing a post-treatment cancer 100% without § 3.105(e) 60-day notice under DC 7528 Note (Foster v. McDonough, 34 Vet. App. 338 (2021), which enforces § 3.105(e) notice while holding §§ 3.343/3.344 stabilized-rating rules inapplicable to temporary cancer discontinuances)—is void ab initio!

trapTables.title: 3. Traumatic Brain Injury (DC 8045): Two-Era Historical Diff (1946 vs. Oct. 23, 2008)
headers: Era 2: October 23, 2008 – Present (73 FR 54693, pub. Sept. 23, 2008; 73 FR 69554; 79 FR 45093)
rows: Core Architecture
Split strictly between (1) Purely neurological disabilities (hemiplegia, cranial nerve paralysis, epilepsies) vs. (2) Purely subjective symptomatology (DC 8045-9304).
Evaluates three main areas of dysfunction: (1) Cognitive, (2) Emotional/Behavioral, and (3) Physical (including subjective symptoms).
Cognitive & Subjective Rating Ceiling

Hard 10% Ceiling Trap: Purely subjective complaints recognized as symptomatic of brain trauma (headaches, dizziness, insomnia, memory/concentration complaints) were capped at 10% under DC 9304, and could NOT be combined with any other brain-trauma rating in the absence of a diagnosis of multi-infarct dementia!

10-Facet Table (0% / 10% / 40% / 70% / 100%): Evaluates cognitive impairment and subjective symptoms across 10 facets scored 0, 1, 2, 3, or Total. Highest-Facet Rule: The veteran's DC 8045 percentage equals the highest level assigned on ANY single facet (0 = 0%, 1 = 10%, 2 = 40%, 3 = 70%, Total = 100%)—never an average or sum!
The 10 Evaluated Facets
None (unstructured DC 9304 dementia schedule if organic dementia proven; otherwise 10% max).

1. Memory, attention, concentration, executive functions (0–Total) · 2. Judgment (0–Total) · 3. Social interaction (caps at Level 3 = 70% via 0–3) · 4. Orientation (0–Total) · 5. Motor activity (with intact motor/sensory system — apraxia/initiation) (0–Total) · 6. Visual-spatial orientation (0–Total) · 7. Subjective symptoms (cluster of headaches/dizziness/fatigue/malaise not otherwise separately rated; caps at Level 2 = 40% via 0–2) · 8. Neurobehavioral effects (irritability, impulsivity, unpredictability, aggression; caps at Level 3 = 70% via 0–3) · 9. Communication (comprehension/expression; 0–Total: 0/1/2/3/Total) · 10. Consciousness (persistent vegetative state or coma = Total (100%) only).
Co-Existing Physical, Mental & Migraine Residuals

Crucial Era-1 CUE Loophole: Separately diagnosed neurological or physical conditions—such as Migraines (8045-8100 up to 50%), Peripheral Vestibular Disorder (8045-6204 up to 30%), Post-Traumatic Epilepsy (8045-8910–8914), cranial nerve palsies, or comorbid PTSD (DC 9411)—were NOT "purely subjective complaints" and had to be rated under their dedicated codes!

Physical/Neurological + Note (1) Overlap Rule: Distinct physical/neurological diagnoses (migraines DC 8100, seizures DC 8910–8914, tinnitus DC 6260, vertigo DC 6204, diplopia DC 6090, endocrine § 4.119, skin/scars § 4.118, bowel/bladder, ED SMC(k)) are rated separately unless the exact same symptom is already used to elevate a DC 8045 facet (§ 4.14). Under Note (1), comorbid mental disorders (§ 4.130) are rated separately unless manifestations cannot be delineated without speculation (Mittleider v. West, 11 Vet. App. 181 (1998)), in which case VA assigns a single combined evaluation under whichever schedule yields the higher rating (Playbook 18).
Governing Notes (2)–(5)
N/A

• Note (2): Listed facet symptoms are illustrative examples, NOT mandatory cumulative checklists. · • Note (3): Distinguishes basic ADLs from IADLs (finances, shopping, meal prep, medication management, travel). · • Note (4): Initial in-service TBI severity label ("mild", "moderate", "severe" based on acute Glasgow Coma Scale / LOC / PTA) does NOT cap or control current residual ratings (though initial severity DOES govern § 3.310(d) secondary presumptions!). · • Note (5): Allowed veterans rated at 10% pre-Oct. 23, 2008 to request review under the new table without proving worsening.

trapTables.title: A. Migraines (DC 8100) — Controlling Precedential Matrix
rows: "With very frequent completely prostrating and prolonged attacks productive of severe economic inadaptability"

• Pierce v. Principi, 18 Vet. App. 440, 445–46 (2004): "Productive of" means capable of producing (NOT necessarily currently producing complete job loss); "severe economic inadaptability" denotes substantial work impairment (missed workdays, leaving shifts early, FMLA/sick-leave exhaustion, workplace accommodations, inability to work during attacks)—continued full-time employment does NOT bar 50%! · • Johnson v. Wilkie, 30 Vet. App. 245, 250–55 (2018): DC 8100 tiers are successive and conjunctive (making § 4.7 "nearly approximates" inapplicable across missing elements), so 50% requires (1) very frequent (>1/month, contrasted against 30% once/month), (2) completely prostrating (extreme exhaustion/powerlessness compelling cessation of activity), (3) prolonged, AND (4) productive of severe economic inadaptability. Crucially, the Board cannot invent arbitrary, undisclosed numerical thresholds (e.g., demanding weekly attacks or >48-hour duration) without articulating a reasoned medical or dictionary basis! · • Ingram v. Collins, 38 Vet. App. 130 (2025): Because DC 8100 is completely silent on medication, raters and examiners cannot discount baseline migraine frequency, prostration, or duration based on ameliorative relief from abortive/prophylactic medications (sumatriptan/rizatriptan, gepants, CGRP monoclonal antibodies, Botox, topiramate, propranolol)! (Watchlist: VA's Feb. 17, 2026 § 4.10 IFR at 91 FR 7118 was rescinded ab initio Feb. 27, 2026 at 91 FR 9712).
"With characteristic prostrating attacks occurring on an average once a month over last several months"
Requires characteristic prostrating attacks averaging 1 per month over the last several months (no economic-inadaptability requirement).
"With characteristic prostrating attacks averaging one in 2 months over last several months"
Averages 1 prostrating attack every 2 months over the last several months.
"With less frequent attacks"
Diagnosed SC migraines/headaches with prostrating attacks less frequent than once every 2 months (or non-prostrating headaches).

Brown, 7 Vet. App. 95 (1994) — CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive)! · • Also check 100% psychoneurotic disjunctive prong ("or demonstrably unable to obtain or retain employment"; Gleicher, 2 Vet. App. 26; Mitchem, 9 Vet. App. 138).
Era 3: Nov. 7, 1996 – Aug. 3, 2014 (61 FR 52695 DSM-IV Overhaul)

Era 4: Aug. 4, 2014 – Present (79 FR 45093 DSM-5 Alignment)

trapTables.title: A. Controlling Precedential Architecture on § 4.130 (0% / 10% / 30% / 50% / 70% / 100%)
rows: Mauerhan v. Principi, 16 Vet. App. 436 (2002)

The phrase "such symptoms as" makes the listed symptoms at each tier (30%, 50%, 70%, 100%) non-exhaustive illustrative examples—raters may neither treat them as a mandatory cumulative checklist nor deny a higher tier when unenumerated symptoms produce equivalent occupational and social impairment.
Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) pre-2002; binding on all open/AMA claims.
Vazquez-Claudio v. Shinseki, 713 F.3d 112 (Fed. Cir. 2013)

§ 4.130 is predominantly symptom-driven: evaluating a mental disorder is a two-part inquiry assessing (1) what symptoms exist, AND (2) their frequency, severity, and duration (§ 4.126(a)) to determine the resulting level of occupational and social impairment ("deficiencies in most areas" at 70% vs. "reduced reliability and productivity" at 50%).
Binding Federal Circuit holistic test.
Bankhead v. Shulkin, 29 Vet. App. 10, 20–22 (2017) & Golden v. Shulkin, 29 Vet. App. 221 (2018)

Suicidal Ideation = 70% Hallmark: The presence of suicidal ideation alone—including passive suicidal ideation (thoughts of one's own death or wishing to be dead)—signals 70%-level impairment without requiring active intent, a lethal plan, preparatory acts, or inpatient psychiatric hospitalization! If the Board assigns < 70% despite documented suicidal ideation, it must explain why the veteran's overall symptom profile fails to approximate 70%. (Golden reinforces alignment with DSM-5 symptom definitions).
Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) against final pre-2017 decisions; premier direct-appeal / HLR / Board remand weapon!
Sellers v. Principi, 372 F.3d 1318 (Fed. Cir. 2004) & Amberman v. Shinseki, 570 F.3d 1377 (Fed. Cir. 2009)

Single Mental Rating Consolidation (§ 4.14): All comorbid DC 9201–9440 psychiatric diagnoses (e.g., DC 9411 PTSD + DC 9434 MDD + DC 9400 GAD + DC 9421 Somatic Symptom Disorder + secondary substance-use disorder under Allen v. Principi) are consolidated into ONE combined § 4.130 rating reflecting total psychiatric impairment. (See Section 3.C for mandatory separate physical/neurological/eating-disorder carve-outs!)
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (>= Nov. 7, 1996).
McCarroll v. McDonald, 28 Vet. App. 267 (2016) (en banc) vs. Ingram v. Collins, 38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)

Psychotropic Medication Rule: § 4.130's 0% and 10% tiers explicitly mention continuous medication ("or symptoms controlled by continuous medication" = 10%), whereas 30%, 50%, 70%, and 100% are silent on medication. Thus, if SSRIs/mood stabilizers genuinely control symptoms down to mild/asymptomatic levels, 10% applies (McCarroll); however, whenever residual symptoms persist above 10% (panic attacks, depressed mood, sleep impairment, suicidal ideation), 30%–100% are silent on medication, barring examiners from discounting partially medicated severity under Ingram (91 FR 7118 rescinded 91 FR 9712)!
Audit both § 4.130 residual severity AND secondary medication side-effect claims!

trapTables.title: A. Functional Loss on Repetition, Flare-Ups & C&P Testing (§§ 4.40, 4.45, 4.59)
rows: DeLuca v. Brown, 8 Vet. App. 202, 205–07 (1995)

Diagnostic codes predicated on limitation of motion (DC 5201, 5206–5207, 5251–5252, 5260–5261, 5271, 5235–5243) are not capped by single-pass passive goniometer arcs: VA must evaluate additional functional loss caused by weakness, fatigability, incoordination, or pain on repetitive use and express that loss in terms of equivalent additional ROM degrees lost.

Open-Claim / Appeal Remand Engine: An examiner's failure to record DeLuca repetitive-use loss is an inadequate-exam / duty-to-assist error, which cannot constitute CUE under Cook v. Principi, 318 F.3d 1334 (Fed. Cir. 2002) (en banc) (unless the C&P report already quantified the exact post-repetition/flare ROM degrees meeting a higher tier and the rater ignored them!).
Mitchell v. Shinseki, 25 Vet. App. 32, 40–44 (2011)

Pain alone does not automatically equal the limitation-of-motion degrees at which pain begins! For pain during motion (e.g., knee flexion pain starting at 90° with full movement to 130°) to trigger a higher ROM tier (DC 5260 <= 45°), the medical/lay evidence must show pain causes functional loss equivalent to inability to perform movement beyond the compensable ROM cutoff (e.g., pain preventing weight-bearing, squatting, or repetitive flexion past 45°).

Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE): Defeats naive CUE claims arguing "pain began at 30° flexion = automatic 20% DC 5260" where full active motion persisted without equivalent functional loss.
Sharp v. Shulkin, 29 Vet. App. 26, 32–36 (2017)

C&P examiners must elicit flare-up frequency, duration, and functional impairment from the veteran and provide a medical estimate of additional ROM loss during flares—even when the exam is not conducted during an active flare—unless the examiner explains why medical knowledge as a whole (not personal reluctance or lack of contemporaneous observation) renders any estimate speculative.
Open-Claim Only (Cook CUE Bar): Classic Board/CAVC remand hook against boilerplate "cannot estimate flare-up loss without mere speculation because veteran not examined during flare" DBQs.
Correia v. McDonald, 28 Vet. App. 158, 166–70 (2016)
Final sentence of § 4.59

To be adequate, a joint examination must (where feasible) test and record ROM across four modalities on both the affected and opposite undamaged joint: (1) active motion, (2) passive motion, (3) weight-bearing, and (4) nonweight-bearing.
Open-Claim Only (Cook CUE Bar): Never plead a Correia missing-modality DBQ defect as RO/Board CUE—file a Supplemental Claim, HLR, or Board/CAVC remand!

trapTables.title: A. Multi-Joint Active Inflammatory Arthritis (DC 5002) vs. Degenerative / Post-Traumatic Arthritis (DC 5003 & DC 5010)
rows: Core Evaluation Pathways

Rated EITHER (whichever is higher—never combined!): · 1. Active Process: · • 100%: Constitutional manifestations associated with active joint involvement, totally incapacitating. · • 60%: Less than criteria for 100% with weight loss and anemia productive of severe impairment of health, OR 4 or more incapacitating exacerbations/year. · • 40%: Symptom combinations productive of definite impairment of health objectively supported by examination, OR 3 or more incapacitating exacerbations/year. · • 20%: 1 or 2 exacerbations/year in a well-established diagnosis. · OR 2. Chronic Residuals: Rate each affected joint separately on limitation of motion / ankylosis / § 4.59 painful motion (DC 5003 post-2021 Note 1) and combine under § 4.25 (+ § 4.26 bilateral factor)!

1. Compensable ROM or § 4.59 Painful Motion Present (DC 5003 & DC 5010): Rate each affected joint separately under its dedicated § 4.71a joint code (DC 5201, 5252, 5260, 5271, etc.)—including 10% (or 20% shoulder) per joint for objective painful motion under § 4.59 (Lichtenfels v. Derwinski, 1 Vet. App. 484, 488 (1991)). (Note: Effective Feb. 7, 2021 at 85 FR 76453, DC 5010 Post-Traumatic Arthritis directs rating directly under affected joint limitation/dislocation/instability codes combined under § 4.25, decoupling DC 5010 from DC 5003's X-ray fallback below). · 2. DC 5003 Fallback Multi-Joint X-Ray Rule (ONLY When Affected Joints Have 0% Noncompensable ROM AND Zero Painful Motion): · • 10%: "X-ray findings" (MRI/CT accepted administratively under M21-1) showing involvement of 2 or more major joints OR 2 or more minor joint groups. · • 20%: Involvement of 2 or more major joints OR 2 or more minor joint groups, with occasional incapacitating exacerbations.
Critical § 4.14 Anti-Pyramiding Trap

DC 5002 Note: Chronic residual joint ratings and active-process ratings cannot be combined (§ 4.14)—VA must calculate both pathways and award whichever yields the higher combined evaluation! (Systemic extra-articular manifestations—e.g., uveitis, interstitial lung disease, rheumatoid nodules, biologic skin/immunosuppression—are rated separately if non-overlapping).

DC 5003 Note (1): The 10% and 20% multi-joint imaging ratings are never combined with compensable limitation-of-motion ratings active on those same joints; they apply only as a fallback floor across remaining 0% non-painful arthritic joints!

trapTables.title: A. Side-by-Side Pre-Feb. 7, 2021 vs. Post-Feb. 7, 2021 Comparison Matrix
headers: Era 2: On or After February 7, 2021 (85 FR 76453 & 86 FR 8142)
rows: DC 5054 (Hip Replacement) & DC 5055 (Knee Replacement)

• Temporary 100%: 1 year (12 months) following implantation of prosthesis (commencing after the initial 1-month § 4.30 post-discharge total rating = 13 months total 100%). · • Minimum Floor: 30% (50%/70%/90% Hip; 60% Knee for chronic severe painful motion/weakness). · • Partial Knee Replacements (Hudgens Window): Covered partial/unicompartmental knee replacements prior to July 16, 2015!

• Temporary 100% Slashed: Cut from 1 year down to 4 months following implantation of prosthesis or joint resurfacing (after 1-month § 4.30 grant = 5 months total 100% per Note 5!). · • Minimum Floor: 30% retained for prosthetic replacement (resurfacing is rated on ROM residuals under 5250–5255 or 5260–5262 after 4 months without the 30% prosthesis floor). · • Note 2 (Revisions): Revision surgery earns 4-month 100% only if all original components are replaced (partial revision uses § 4.30). (Note: Shoulder 5051, Elbow 5052, Wrist 5053, and Ankle 5056 retained 1 year 100%!)
DC 5257 (Knee Instability & Patellofemoral Complex)
Subjective three-tier scale for "Recurrent subluxation or lateral instability": Severe 30%, Moderate 20%, Slight 10% (no brace or prescription device required; patellar subluxation often disputed).

Objective repair + prescribed device tiers + Patellofemoral Note: · • 10%: Sprain, incomplete ligament tear, or complete tear (repaired/unrepaired/failed) with persistent instability without prescribed assistive device/bracing. · • 20%: Sprain, incomplete tear, or repaired complete tear with persistent instability AND medical provider prescribes brace AND/OR assistive device (cane/crutches/walker). · • 30%: Unrepaired or failed repair of complete ligament tear with persistent instability AND medical provider prescribes BOTH an assistive device AND bracing. · • Patellofemoral Complex Note: Recurrent patellar/retropatellar instability (10% w/ or w/o surgery; 20% post-surgery + prescribed brace or cane/walker; 30% post-surgery + prescribed brace AND cane/walker).
DC 5269 (Plantar Fasciitis — Corrected from DC 5285!)
No dedicated DC! Rated by analogy (§ 4.20)—most favorably under DC 5276 (Flatfoot) up to 30% unilateral / 50% bilateral, or DC 5284 (10/20/30%).

Dedicated DC 5269 (initially printed as DC 5285 in 85 FR 76453, formally corrected Feb. 4, 2021 at 86 FR 8142 to DC 5269 to prevent colliding with legacy pre-2003 DC 5285 Vertebral Fracture!): · • 10%: Otherwise, unilateral or bilateral. · • 20%: Unilateral, no relief from BOTH non-surgical AND surgical treatment. · • 30%: Bilateral, no relief from BOTH non-surgical AND surgical treatment (Note 2: if recommended for surgery but not a surgical candidate, rate at 20% or 30%!). · • 40% (DC 5167): With actual loss of use of the foot (+ mandatory SMC(k)!).
DC 5271 (Ankle, Limited Motion)
Qualitative adjectives only: Marked 20%, Moderate 10% (M21-1 degree benchmarks were non-binding on BVA).
Codified explicit goniometer thresholds: · • 20% (Marked): Dorsiflexion < 5° OR plantar flexion < 10°. · • 10% (Moderate): Dorsiflexion < 15° OR plantar flexion < 30°.
DC 5262 (Tibia & Fibula / Shin Splints)
Malunion rated on "slight 10% / moderate 20% / marked 30% knee or ankle disability"; no explicit shin-splints text.

Malunion rated directly under DC 5256, 5257, 5260, or 5261 (knee) or DC 5270 or 5271 (ankle) (highest); added explicit Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (MTSS / shin splints) tiers (0% / 10% / 20% / 30%).
DC 5000 (Osteomyelitis)
Historical 5-year cure/discontinuance trap & qualitative active/inactive rules; DC 5000 Note allowed discontinuing 10% inactive rating after 5 years cure.

Retained 10/20/30/60/100% osteomyelitis tiers (100% pelvis/vertebrae/major joints/constitutional; 60% frequent constitutional episodes; 30% involucrum/sequestrum; 20% discharging sinus or active infection within 5 yrs; 10% inactive following repeated episodes), modernized infectious/surgical cross-references.
DC 5012 (Malignant Bone Neoplasm) & DC 5244 (Paralysis)
DC 5012: 100% active + 1 year post-cessation of treatment; no DC 5244 in Spine block.

DC 5012 retitled "Bones, neoplasm, malignant, primary or secondary" (100% + 1 year post-cessation of surgery/chemo/radiation, then residuals); added DC 5244 (Traumatic paralysis, complete or incomplete) cross-referencing DC 5109–5111 / peripheral nerves + SMC.

trapTables.title: 1. Master Chronological Federal Register & Precedent Ledger (1946–2026)
rows: Established baseline §§ 4.96–4.97 (DC 6501–6821): qualitative dyspnea/attack descriptors for bronchitis, asthma, emphysema, bronchiectasis, and active/inactive tuberculosis (§§ 4.96(b)–(c)). No diagnostic code existed for Sleep Apnea.
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (< Oct. 7, 1996): Governs all pre-Oct. 7, 1996 respiratory ratings; pre-1996 Sleep Apnea was rated by analogy (§ 4.20) under DC 6800, 6516, or 8108.

Comprehensive Respiratory Overhaul: First complete revision since 1945. Enacted § 4.96(a) coexisting-rating bar (DC 6600–6817 & 6822–6847) with upper-airway (6502–6524) carve-out; introduced FEV-1/FVC/DLCO(SB) PFT schedules; modernized Sinusitis (6510–6514), Rhinitis (6522–6524 30% polyps), Asthma (6602 inhaler/steroid tiers), COPD (6604), Interstitial/Restrictive (6825–6845), Sarcoidosis (6846); and created DC 6847 Sleep Apnea Syndromes (0/30/50/100%).

CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (>= Oct. 7, 1996): Plain-text misapplication of § 4.96(a) (e.g., subsuming DC 6510 or 6522 into 6602/6847), ignoring DC 6522 polyps (30%), or ignoring DC 6602 daily inhaled steroids (30%) is undebatable CUE on/after Oct. 7, 1996. Zero CUE reach before Oct. 7, 1996.

71 FR 28586 made technical updates to § 4.97; 71 FR 52457, 52459 added 38 C.F.R. § 4.96(d)(1)–(7) codifying when PFTs/DLCO/post-bronchodilator studies are required or excused, resolving PFT metric disparities ((d)(6)), and barring compensable FEV-1/FVC ratings when both FEV-1 and FVC exceed 100% ((d)(7)).
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (>= Oct. 6, 2006 for § 4.96(d)(1)–(7)): Plain-text § 4.96(d) PFT rules govern decisions rendered on or after Oct. 6, 2006.

trapTables.title: 2. Two-Era Architectural Comparison: Pre- vs. Post-October 7, 1996 (61 FR 46720)
headers: Era 2: October 7, 1996 – Present (61 FR 46720, pub. Sept. 5, 1996)
rows: Pulmonary Assessment Method
Subjective clinical descriptors ("mild," "moderate," "moderately severe," "severe" dyspnea on exertion, cyanosis, frequency/severity of asthmatic paroxysms, purulent expectoration).

Objective Pulmonary Function Testing (PFT) (FEV-1 % predicted, FEV-1/FVC ratio, DLCO(SB) % predicted, VO2 max exercise capacity), outpatient oxygen, cor pulmonale/PH, or explicit medication regimens (§ 4.96(d)).
Sleep Apnea (DC 6847)

No dedicated Diagnostic Code. Rated by analogy (38 C.F.R. § 4.20)—most commonly 6899-6800 (anthracosis/pneumoconiosis), 6599-6516 (chronic laryngitis), or 8199-8108 (narcolepsy / petit mal epilepsy DC 8911).

Dedicated DC 6847 (Sleep Apnea Syndromes: Obstructive, Central, Mixed): 0% asymptomatic -> 30% persistent daytime hypersomnolence -> 50% requires breathing assistance device (CPAP) -> 100% chronic respiratory failure w/ CO2 retention, cor pulmonale, or tracheostomy.
Bronchial Asthma (DC 6602)

Rated on frequency of "characteristic asthmatic attacks" (10% mild/infrequent; 30% moderate w/ weekly/biweekly attacks; 60% severe w/ frequent attacks & moderate dyspnea; 100% pronounced w/ emphysema/right-heart strain).

Objective disjunctive ("or") matrix: FEV-1 (10/30/60/100%) OR FEV-1/FVC OR medication tier (10% intermittent bronchodilator; 30% daily bronchodilator or inhaled anti-inflammatory; 60% >=3/yr systemic steroid courses; 100% daily high-dose systemic steroids).
Chronic COPD (DC 6604)
Split across DC 6600 (Bronchitis), DC 6603 (Emphysema), and DC 6601 (Bronchiectasis); no unified DC 6604 COPD code.
Added DC 6604 (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease) evaluated alongside DC 6600 and DC 6603 under the General Rating Formula for DC 6600, 6603, 6604.
Tuberculosis (DC 6701–6732)
Legacy active/arrested ratings (DC 6701–6724) + statutory graduated two-year 100% -> 50% -> 30% protections for pre-Aug. 19, 1968 awards (§ 3.959, §§ 4.96(b)–(c)).

Retained §§ 4.96(b)–(c) savings rules for legacy TB while adding modern DC 6730 (Chronic pulmonary TB, active = 100%) and DC 6731 (Chronic pulmonary TB, inactive = residuals) (1-yr active 100% treatment rule under Note).
Coexisting Rating Bar (§ 4.96(a))
Broad anti-pyramiding warnings against combining bronchitis, bronchiectasis, asthma, and emphysema.
Codified exact numerical range lock in 38 C.F.R. § 4.96(a): bars combining DC 6600–6817 and 6822–6847 (plus 6819–6820 when lung/pleura involved), explicitly leaving DC 6502–6524 outside the bar!

trapTables.title: A. Exact Scope of the § 4.96(a) Single-Rating Lock
rows: DC 6502–6524 (Nose, Sinuses, Larynx & Pharynx)

Deviated septum (6502), Nasal loss (6504), Sinusitis (6510–6514), Laryngitis (6515–6516), Laryngectomy/Aphonia (6518–6519), Stenosis (6520), Pharynx (6521), Allergic/Bacterial/Granulomatous Rhinitis (6522–6524)

EXEMPT FROM § 4.96(a)! May be rated separately from each other AND separately alongside any lower-respiratory or Sleep Apnea code (DC 6600–6847), subject only to 38 C.F.R. § 4.14 against compensating the exact same symptom twice (Esteban v. Brown, 6 Vet. App. 259 (1994)).
DC 6600–6817 & DC 6822–6847 (Trachea/Bronchi, TB, Vascular, Mycotic, Interstitial, Restrictive, Sarcoidosis & Sleep Apnea)

Bronchitis (6600), Bronchiectasis (6601), Asthma (6602), Emphysema (6603), COPD (6604), TB (6701–6731), Pulmonary Vascular (6817), Actinomycosis/Mycotic (6822–6839), Interstitial (6825–6833), Restrictive (6840–6845), Sarcoidosis (6846), Sleep Apnea (6847)

STRICTLY NON-COMBINABLE WITH EACH OTHER. Assign ONE single rating under the DC reflecting the predominant disability, with elevation to the next higher evaluation where the severity of the overall respiratory disability warrants such elevation.
DC 6819–6820 (Malignant & Benign Respiratory Neoplasms)
Lung/bronchial cancer, pleural mesothelioma (6819), laryngeal/tracheal/sinus carcinoma (6819), benign respiratory neoplasms (6820)

• With lung or pleural involvement: Cannot combine 6819 & 6820 with each other OR with DC 6600–6817 / 6822–6847. · • WITHOUT lung or pleural involvement (e.g., upper-airway paranasal sinus or laryngeal neoplasm): OUTSIDE the § 4.96(a) lower-lung combination bar!

trapTables.title: A. Nose, Sinuses, Larynx & Pharynx Reference Schedule
headers: Rating Tiers & Critical Regulatory / Clinical Distinctions
rows: Septum, nasal, deviation of (traumatic only)

10% for traumatic deviation with >= 50% obstruction of nasal passage on BOTH sides OR complete (100%) obstruction on ONE side (0% if below threshold; developmental/congenital septal deviation without in-service trauma is non-compensable unless aggravated or surgically altered).
Nose, loss of part of, or scars

30% when both nasal passages are exposed (loss of alae/tip exposing nares); 10% for loss of part of one ala or other obvious disfigurement. Special Note: Also evaluate under DC 7800 Scars/Disfigurement of Head, Face, or Neck (10%–80%) and assign whichever higher or non-duplicative rating applies (Scars Diff)!
Chronic Sinusitis: · • 6510 Pansinusitis · • 6511 Ethmoid · • 6512 Frontal · • 6513 Maxillary · • 6514 Sphenoid

General Rating Formula for Sinusitis (DC 6510–6514): · • 50%: Following radical surgery with chronic osteomyelitis, OR near-constant sinusitis characterized by headaches, pain and tenderness of affected sinus, and purulent discharge or crusting after repeated surgeries. · • 30%: >= 3 incapacitating episodes/year requiring prolonged (4 to 6 weeks) antibiotic treatment, OR > 6 non-incapacitating episodes/year characterized by headaches, pain, and purulent discharge or crusting. · • 10%: 1 or 2 incapacitating episodes/year requiring prolonged (4–6 wks) antibiotic treatment, OR 3 to 6 non-incapacitating episodes/year characterized by headaches, pain, and purulent discharge or crusting. · • 0%: Detected by X-ray (or CT) only.
Laryngitis: Tuberculous (6515) / Chronic (6516)
• 30%: Hoarseness, with thickening or nodules of cords, polyps, submucous infiltration, or pre-malignant changes on biopsy. · • 10%: Hoarseness, with inflammation of cords or mucous membrane.
Laryngectomy, total

Flat 100% + MANDATORY SMC(k) under 38 U.S.C. § 1114(k) / 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)(6) for complete organic aphonia! (Protected from post-surgical reduction under Note; omitting SMC(k) on a DC 6518 award is textbook plain-text RO CUE!)
Aphonia, complete organic

• 100%: Constant inability to communicate by speech (unable to communicate even by whisper) + MANDATORY SMC(k) (§ 3.350(a)(6))! · • 60%: Constant inability to speak above a whisper. · • Note: Evaluate incomplete aphonia as chronic laryngitis (DC 6516), and refer to § 4.96(c) for special monthly compensation.
Larynx, stenosis of (6520); Pharynx, injuries to (6521)

• 6520: 100%/60%/30%/10% via FEV-1 flow-volume loop (<40%, 40–55%, 56–70%, 71–80% + inspiratory flow flattening) or 100% with tracheostomy. · • 6521: 50% for stricture/obstruction of pharynx/nasopharynx, absence of soft palate secondary to trauma/chemical/burn, or paralysis of soft palate with swallowing regurgitation/nasal speech.
Allergic or vasomotor rhinitis

• 30%: With polyps (any nasal polyps documented on anterior rhinoscopy, nasal endoscopy, or sinus CT = automatic 30%, without any obstruction percentage requirement!). · • 10%: Without polyps, but with > 50% obstruction of nasal passage on BOTH sides OR complete (100%) obstruction on ONE side.
Bacterial rhinitis
• 50%: Rhinoscleroma. · • 10%: With permanent hypertrophy of turbinates AND with > 50% obstruction on BOTH sides OR complete (100%) obstruction on ONE side.
Granulomatous rhinitis (PACT § 1120 presumptive!)
• 100%: Wegener's granulomatosis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis — GPA) or lethal midline granuloma. · • 20%: Other types of granulomatous infection (e.g., nasal sarcoidosis, rhinosporidiosis).

title: Schedule for Rating Disabilities (1945 Looseleaf Edition)
summary: Although titled the '1945 Schedule for Rating Disabilities,' the baseline post-WWII VASRD took effect on April 1, 1946 (38 C.F.R. § 3.952; Part 4, Appendix A) and was codified in the Federal Register on May 22, 1964 (29 FR 6718). Protected pre-readjustment awards are governed by 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.951(a), 3.952, and 3.953.
